- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related: ACP node runtime architecture / protocol / verification docs under `docs/experiments/plans/`
- Related: landing-only extension test isolation fixes after rebase onto current `main`

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- OpenClaw now has a first-class ACP node-backed runtime path where the gateway owns durable ACP truth and paired nodes execute the worker role.
- Gateway restart/recovery can resume incomplete ACP outward projection from durable state.
- Duplicate accepted worker-event replay on reconnect is hardened so it does not duplicate outward delivery.
- Post-restart tool updates intentionally follow the documented conservative v1 rule: `append_only_after_restart`.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? Yes
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- New/changed network calls? Yes
- Command/tool execution surface changed? Yes
- Data access scope changed? Yes

### Security / trust-boundary notes

- Paired nodes can now advertise ACP worker capability and receive ACP runtime commands over the existing gateway↔node trust boundary.
- Gateway↔node websocket traffic now carries ACP worker control / event flows in addition to existing node commands.
- Gateway now persists ACP runtime state needed for durable replay/recovery.
- The design mitigates stale-worker / duplicate-delivery risks via lease epochs, canonical terminal resolution, durable replay checkpoints, and reconnect/replay handling on the gateway.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux (landing worktree on vm1) + GitHub Actions CI
- Runtime/container: Node / pnpm; Bun build path also checked
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel (if any): ACP gateway↔node runtime path
- Relevant config (redacted): ACP runtime restart/replay harnesses and paired-node fixtures

### Verified locally

- ACP targeted verification gate:
  - `pnpm test -- src/auto-reply/reply/acp-projector.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.replay.test.ts src/acp/store/store.test.ts src/acp/store/store.restart.test.ts src/acp/store/gateway-events.test.ts src/gateway/server-node-events.acp.test.ts src/gateway/server-startup.acp-node.test.ts src/node-host/invoke-acp.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/nodes.acp.test.ts`
- TypeScript guardrail:
  - `pnpm tsgo`
- Landing-only extension test fixes:
  - `pnpm test:extensions`

### CI / build notes

- `pnpm build` still fails only with the pre-existing Bun wrapper issue:
  - `Cannot find module './cjs/index.cjs' from ''`
- That build failure was already present and is not introduced by the ACP runtime changes in this PR.

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

What I personally verified (not just CI), and how:

- Verified the ACP-focused local gate listed above.
- Verified `pnpm tsgo` passes.
- Verified the rebased landing branch’s extension test-isolation fixes with local `pnpm test:extensions`.
- Verified the PR now includes the architecture / protocol / verification / final-judge docs for this backend.

What I did **not** verify:

- I did **not** get a clean `pnpm build` because of the pre-existing Bun wrapper failure noted above.
- I did **not** run a fresh manual end-to-end Discord/real-node interactive repro outside the checked-in restart/replay and node-host harnesses.

## Review Guide

If you want the shortest path through this PR, review in this order:

1. **Core architecture / intent**
   - `docs/experiments/plans/acp-node-backed-runtime.md`
   - `docs/experiments/plans/acp-node-backed-runtime-protocol.md`
2. **Gateway-owned durable state**
   - `src/acp/store/**`
3. **Node execution bridge**
   - `src/node-host/**`
   - `src/gateway/server-methods/nodes.ts`
   - `src/gateway/server-node-events.ts`
4. **Durable outward replay path**
   - `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.ts`
   - `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.ts`
   - `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-replay.ts`
5. **Recovery and proofs**
   - `src/gateway/server-startup.acp-node.ts`
   - `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.replay.test.ts`
   - `src/gateway/server-startup.acp-node.test.ts`
6. **Ignore as landing-only test fixes unless you are checking CI fallout**
   - `extensions/feishu/**`
   - `extensions/google/**`
   - `extensions/googlechat/**`

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

If a bot review conversation is addressed by this PR, resolve that conversation yourself. Do not leave bot review conversation cleanup for maintainers.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config/env changes? No explicit migration required
- Migration needed? No

Notes:

- This adds a new ACP runtime/backend path; it does not force existing deployments to switch to it immediately.
- Post-restart tool updates intentionally remain append-only in v1.

## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)

- How to disable/revert this change quickly: revert this PR or avoid selecting/using the `acp-node` runtime path until fixed.
- Files/config to restore: ACP runtime/store/gateway/node-host changes under `src/acp/**`, `src/node-host/**`, `src/gateway/**`, plus the accompanying docs if reverting wholesale.
- Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: duplicate final delivery after restart, stale worker winning after reconnect, projector checkpoint drift, or replay targeting the wrong route.

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: restart/replay correctness is subtle in any durable projection system.
  - Mitigation: this PR includes restart harnesses, startup recovery tests, reconnect/replay ordering tests, and explicit protocol/verification docs.
- Risk: the PR is large and spans multiple ACP runtime layers.
  - Mitigation: the review guide above splits it into durable store, node bridge, replay path, recovery path, and landing-only CI fixes.
- Risk: paired-node ACP execution expands the gateway↔node command surface.
  - Mitigation: the gateway remains authoritative for leases, terminal resolution, checkpoints, and replay instead of trusting node-local completion.

Verify transcript flow, reply actions, session switching, settings, direct mode, phone-proxy mode, tile/complication entry points, and reopen/background behavior. 3. Send assistant replies while the watch app is foregrounded and backgrounded, then verify reply notifications, quick reply, reconnect/disconnect behavior, and latest-message scrolling. ### Expected - The watch should show a compact, reliable chat UX with correct connection state, preserved transcript state, working reply paths, and background reply notifications. ### Actual - Matches expected in manual testing on Pixel Watch 2 and both small/large Wear emulators. ## Evidence Attach at least one: - [ ] Failing test/log before + passing after - [ ] Trace/log snippets - [x] Screenshot/recording - [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant) Actual screenshots from Pixel Watch 2: | | | | |---|---|---| | Empty tanscript view | Empty transcript view | Swipe over to menu | | Scroll down in menu | Scroll further down | Click behavior settings button | | Scroll down | Click screen awake setting | Click screen awake setting again | | Go back and enter connection settings | Scroll down to helper text | Disable phone proxy | | Scroll down to gateway config | Scroll further down | Go back to transcript view | | Scroll down to see reply edge button (*default view* if you open the app≈) | Reply button toggles voice input (or let's you pick first, if disabled in settings) | Thinking animation | | When closing app, notification is delivered| Tile adding dialog with preview of tile | Actual tile | | Watch face with complication at top and bottom right (different formats) | ## Human Verification (required) What you personally verified (not just CI), and how: - Verified scenarios: Manually tested on a Pixel Watch 2 via Tailscale phone proxy and in both small and large round Wear emulators. Verified chat launch, latest-message behavior, reply flow, session picker, chat settings, connection settings, direct gateway mode, phone-proxy mode, tile launch, complication launch, background reply notifications, and quick reply from the notification. - Edge cases checked: Reopening the app after backgrounding, disconnect/reconnect flow, switching away from and back to the transcript page, scrolling away from latest and jumping back, and testing on both small and large round watch layouts. - What you did **not** verify: every possible Android OEM pairing/background-policy variant, and exhaustive real-network failure cases beyond the implemented reconnect/error handling paths. ## Review Conversations - [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR. - [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment. target.title: feat: add user-specific memory isolation
target.body:
## Summary

Adds user-specific memory isolation to OpenClaw, enabling per-user memory files in multi-user environments.

## Changes

### Core Feature
- **MemoryIsolationConfig** type added to `src/config/types.memory.ts`
  - `isolation.enabled` (default: `true`) to enable/disable isolation

### Session Key Extraction
- **extractUserIdFromSessionKey()** added to `src/sessions/session-key-utils.ts`
  - Extracts userId from direct message session keys
  - Returns `null` for channel/group sessions

### Memory Path Access Control
- **isMemoryPath()** updated in `src/memory/internal.ts`
  - When `userId` is provided, enforces access control
  - Users can only access their own `memory/{userId}/` directory
  - Shared memory files at `memory/` root are accessible to all

### Memory Tools
- **memory_search** and **memory_get** tools updated
  - Accept optional `senderId` parameter
  - Falls back to `senderId` from inbound context when session key doesn't contain userId

### Plugin Integration
- **extensions/memory-core/index.ts** updated
  - Passes `requesterSenderId` from plugin context to memory tools

## How It Works

```
Session Type       | userId Source          | Memory Path
-------------------|------------------------|---------------------------
Direct Message     | sessionKey extraction  | memory/{userId}/YYYY-MM-DD.md
Channel/Group     | requesterSenderId      | memory/{senderId}/YYYY-MM-DD.md
Disabled (legacy)  | none                   | memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md (shared)
```

## Security

- Users cannot access other users' memory directories
- Path validation in `isMemoryPath()` prevents directory traversal
- Shared memory at `memory/` root is accessible to all (for global context)

## Testing

- Unit tests added in `src/memory/internal.test.ts`
- All existing tests pass

## Breaking Changes

None. The feature is opt-in via configuration and defaults to the new isolated behavior when `memory.isolation.enabled` is not set (defaults to `true`).

Users who want the old shared behavior can set:
```json
{
  "memory": {
    "isolation": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

target.title: security: gateway public network hardening
target.body:
## Summary

Implements comprehensive security hardening for OpenClaw Gateway when exposed to public networks (e.g. `https://openclaw.allegro.earth/`). The existing security mechanisms (non-loopback auth enforcement, auth rate limiting, CORS checks) leave gaps that this PR addresses:

- **IP access control** (allowlist/blocklist with CIDR support) — enforced on both HTTP requests and WebSocket upgrades, loopback always allowed, blocklist takes priority
- **Password/token strength validation** — CRITICAL startup warnings when network-exposed with short tokens (<32 chars) or weak passwords (<12 chars, all-digit/all-letter patterns)
- **TLS enforcement check** — CRITICAL startup warning when network-exposed without TLS and no `terminatedUpstream` declaration
- **Per-IP request rate limiting** — sliding window (default 120 req/min/IP), loopback exempt by default, returns 429 with Retry-After
- **Auth audit logging** — JSONL to `~/.openclaw/logs/gateway-auth.jsonl` with file rotation, records `auth_failure`, `auth_success`, `rate_limited`, `ip_blocked` events
- **Auto HSTS** — `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000` set automatically when TLS is enabled
- **Eliminate silent 0.0.0.0 fallback** — `loopback`, `tailnet`, and `custom` bind modes now throw clear errors instead of silently falling back to all-interfaces
- **New security audit checks** — `gateway.no_tls_network_exposed` (critical), `gateway.password_too_short` (critical), `gateway.password_weak_pattern` (warn), `gateway.no_request_rate_limit` (warn), `gateway.auto_bind_fallback` (warn)
- **Enhanced `doctor` warnings** — TLS, password strength, token length, request rate limit checks for network-exposed gateways

### Config additions (`gateway.*`)

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `ipAllowlist` | `string[]` | — | CIDR/IP allowlist (loopback always allowed) |
| `ipBlocklist` | `string[]` | — | CIDR/IP blocklist (checked before allowlist) |
| `requestRateLimit.maxRequests` | `number` | 120 | Max requests per IP per window |
| `requestRateLimit.windowMs` | `number` | 60000 | Sliding window duration (ms) |
| `requestRateLimit.exemptLoopback` | `boolean` | true | Skip rate limiting for localhost |
| `tls.terminatedUpstream` | `boolean` | false | Declare TLS terminated by reverse proxy |

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm tsgo` — type check passes
- [x] New unit tests: `ip-access-control.test.ts` (9 tests), `request-rate-limit.test.ts` (7 tests), `auth-audit-log.test.ts` (4 tests), `credential-strength.test.ts` (9 tests)
- [x] Existing tests updated and passing: `server-runtime-config.test.ts`, `doctor-security.test.ts`, `net.test.ts`, `auth.test.ts`, `audit.test.ts` — 245 tests total
- [ ] Manual: start gateway with `bind=lan` and verify startup warnings
- [ ] Manual: test IP blocklist returns 403
- [ ] Manual: test request rate limit returns 429

target.title: Fix/hooks agent accountid normalization
target.body:
## Summary

Describe the problem and fix in 2–5 bullets:

- Problem: `POST /hooks/agent` silently drops `accountId` from incoming payloads because `HookAgentPayload` lacks the field, `normalizeAgentPayload()` never extracts it, and `dispatchAgentHook()` hand-builds a `CronJob` bypassing `normalizeCronJobCreate()`.
- Why it matters: Multi-account WhatsApp (and any channel requiring `accountId`) delivery fails silently — the caller gets a success response but the message is never sent.
- What changed: Hook dispatch now routes through `normalizeCronJobCreate()`, which promotes legacy flat fields into proper `CronDelivery` with `accountId`. `resolveCronToolPolicy()` derives `disableMessageTool` for shared-contract callers from whether the target is fully resolved (explicit mode + accountId) instead of unconditionally disabling.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): The cron-owned path (`deliveryContract: "cron-owned"`) is untouched. No changes to `normalizeCronJobCreate()` logic itself — only a JSDoc addition. No new config options or API surface.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #43866
- Related #27015, #24186, #42244, #23853, #16925, #30052, #29090

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- `POST /hooks/agent` now correctly preserves `accountId` through to delivery, enabling multi-account WhatsApp delivery via hooks.
- For shared-contract hook runs with a fully resolved delivery target (explicit mode + accountId), the agent's message tool is no longer unconditionally disabled — it remains available as a fallback. The existing `skipMessagingToolDelivery` guard (`run.ts:821-831`) prevents duplicate sends.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? `No`
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No`
- New/changed network calls? `No`
- Command/tool execution surface changed? `No` — the message tool was already available for shared-contract callers without delivery; this change refines *when* it stays enabled based on target resolution quality.
- Data access scope changed? `No`

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: All (server-side code path)
- Runtime/container: Node 22+ / Bun
- Model/provider: Any (not model/provider-specific)
- Integration/channel (if any): WhatsApp (any multi-account channel)
- Relevant config (redacted): Hooks enabled with token, WhatsApp channel configured with multiple `accountId` connections

### Steps

1. Configure two WhatsApp connections with distinct `accountId` values.
2. Send `POST /hooks/agent` with `{ "message": "Hello", "channel": "whatsapp", "to": "1234567890", "accountId": "botnumber" }`.
3. Observe delivery result.

### Expected

- `accountId` flows through to `CronDelivery.accountId`, `resolveDeliveryTarget()` identifies the correct WhatsApp connection, and the message is delivered.

### Actual (before fix)

- `accountId` is silently dropped. Delivery fails because no connection can be identified. Caller receives success response.

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [ ] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

New tests added in second commit:
- `src/gateway/hooks.test.ts` — `normalizeAgentPayload` extracts and trims `accountId` (present, absent, blank)
- `src/gateway/server.hooks.test.ts` — integration test: `accountId` propagates into `job.delivery` via cron normalization pipeline
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.message-tool-policy.test.ts` — 3 tests for shared-contract tool policy: fully resolved target (explicit + accountId → enabled), missing accountId (→ disabled), implicitly resolved target (→ disabled)

Verification: `pnpm tsgo` clean, `pnpm check` clean, all 59 tests across the 4 test files pass.

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: typecheck (`pnpm tsgo`), lint/format (`pnpm check`), unit + integration tests pass for all modified test files
- Edge cases checked: blank/missing `accountId`, `normalizeCronJobCreate` returning null (guard added), implicit vs explicit delivery target mode, `mode: "none"` (verified `deliveryRequested` is already `false` so no extra clause needed)
- What you did **not** verify: live end-to-end delivery through a real WhatsApp multi-account setup; only verified through unit/integration tests and code tracing

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? `Yes`
- Config/env changes? `No`
- Migration needed? `No`

## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)

- How to disable/revert this change quickly: Revert both commits; the hand-built CronJob path is fully self-contained in the reverted `dispatchAgentHook()`.
- Files/config to restore: `src/gateway/hooks.ts`, `src/gateway/server/hooks.ts`, `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.ts`, `src/cron/normalize.ts`
- Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: Hook agent dispatches returning early with "normalizeCronJobCreate returned null" warning (would indicate the normalizer rejects a payload shape it previously accepted via hand-built path).

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: `normalizeCronJobCreate()` could reject a hook payload shape that the hand-built path previously accepted, causing hook dispatches to silently no-op.
  - Mitigation: A null-return guard logs a warning and still returns a `runId` to the caller. The normalizer is well-tested and accepts all fields the hook path provides. Integration test verifies the full pipeline.

- Risk: Enabling the message tool for shared-contract callers with fully resolved targets could cause duplicate sends (agent sends via tool + automatic delivery sends again).
  - Mitigation: The existing `skipMessagingToolDelivery` guard (`run.ts:821-831`) already detects when the agent's message tool sent to the same target and skips automatic delivery. This guard predates this change and is tested.

target.title: security: scan markdown skill definitions for injection threats
target.body:
## Summary

The skill scanner (`src/security/skill-scanner.ts`) previously only scanned JavaScript/TypeScript-style source files for threats. This PR extends it to also scan Markdown `.md` files, including `SKILL.md` definitions, for injection and obfuscation patterns.

Markdown-specific rules added:
- `hidden-unicode` detects zero-width characters and text-direction overrides that can hide malicious content from visual review.
- `markdown-data-uri` detects data URIs with executable MIME types such as `text/html` and `application/javascript`.
- `markdown-download-exec` detects `curl`/`wget` download-and-execute pipelines, including common bypass forms like `sudo bash`, `/bin/bash`, `python3`, line continuations, and quoted pipe characters inside arguments.
- `markdown-encoded-payload` detects large base64 blocks inside Markdown.
- `markdown-hex-payload` detects hex-encoded payloads inside Markdown.

Implementation notes:
- Added `MARKDOWN_EXTENSIONS` and `isMarkdown()`.
- Added `.md` to `SCANNABLE_EXTENSIONS`.
- Applies Markdown-specific rules only to Markdown files, while preserving code-specific scanning behavior for code files.
- Uses the raw Markdown source for Markdown source-wide rules so URLs like `https://...` are not accidentally truncated by code-comment stripping.
- Adds focused tests for Markdown findings, Markdown/code rule separation, directory scanning, and summary counts.

Why this matters: skill definitions can include rendered Markdown. Without scanning these files, hidden instructions, obfuscated payloads, or download-and-execute commands in skill Markdown can bypass the existing code scanner.

Supersedes #10705 (auto-closed by stale bot). Rebased cleanly onto current `main`.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm test src/security/skill-scanner.test.ts`
- [x] `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 CHANGELOG.md src/security/skill-scanner.ts src/security/skill-scanner.test.ts`
- [x] `pnpm check:changed`
- [x] Direct scanner smoke for Markdown download-and-execute bypass forms plus benign Markdown prose and table negative cases

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: Markdown skill definitions such as `SKILL.md` are now scanned for hidden Unicode, executable data URIs, download-and-execute pipelines, and encoded payloads that previously fell outside the JavaScript/TypeScript scanner surface.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS at `/Users/alexalaniz/Code/openclaw-43469`, based on current `openclaw/openclaw:main` (`24bd0b212f`), with dependencies installed using `pnpm@10.33.2`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Ran the actual scanner through `node node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs` against Markdown sources containing `curl`/`wget` bypass forms, then ran `pnpm test src/security/skill-scanner.test.ts`, `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 CHANGELOG.md src/security/skill-scanner.ts src/security/skill-scanner.test.ts`, and `pnpm check:changed`.

Evidence after fix: Copied live terminal output from the local OpenClaw checkout:

```text
markdown scanner smoke passed 7 positives and 2 negatives

Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  32 passed (32)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 3.08s

All matched files use the correct format.

Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
runtime-sidecar-loaders: local runtime sidecar loaders look OK.
Import cycle check: 0 runtime value cycle(s).
```

Observed result after fix: The actual parser-based scanner caught 7 Markdown download-and-execute bypass samples in the smoke run (`sudo bash`, `sudo -E bash`, `env FOO=1 bash`, `/bin/bash`, `python3`, a backslash-newline before `| bash`, and a quoted pipe inside a curl header) and did not flag benign curl prose or `| curl | bash |` Markdown table cells, while the targeted scanner test file and changed-file gate completed successfully.

What was not tested: No known gaps.

target.title: feat(pairing): add configurable pairingMessage text per channel (#41058)
target.body:
## Summary

Adds optional `pairingMessage` config to iMessage and Telegram channel configs, allowing operators to customize or suppress OpenClaw branding in pairing challenge messages sent to unknown senders.

Fixes #41058

## Problem

When `dmPolicy: pairing` is set, every unknown sender receives a hardcoded message exposing:
1. The OpenClaw brand name
2. The channel platform ("Your iMessage sender id:" / "Your Telegram user id:")
3. The full CLI invocation syntax (`openclaw pairing approve imessage CODE`)

No config option exists to override any part of this. The only workaround is patching compiled dist bundles after every update — not sustainable for white-label or privacy-conscious deployments.

## What changed

- `src/pairing/pairing-messages.ts`: Add `PairingMessageConfig` type with optional fields (`header`, `senderIdLabel`, `codeLabel`, `footer`, `showCliHint`). Update `buildPairingReply` to use config when provided.
- `src/config/types.imessage.ts`: Add `pairingMessage?: PairingMessageConfig`
- `src/config/types.telegram.ts`: Add `pairingMessage?: PairingMessageConfig`
- `src/config/zod-schema.providers-core.ts`: Add `PairingMessageConfigSchema`, wire into `IMessageAccountSchemaBase` and `TelegramAccountSchemaBase`
- `src/imessage/monitor/monitor-provider.ts`: Wire `pairingMessage` config into `issuePairingChallenge` via existing `buildReplyText` hook
- `src/telegram/dm-access.ts`: Pass `pairingMessage` through `enforceTelegramDmAccess`, wire into `issuePairingChallenge`
- `src/pairing/pairing-messages.test.ts`: Add tests for all config overrides and backward compat

## Fully backward compatible

All `PairingMessageConfig` fields are optional. Existing deployments with no `pairingMessage` config see zero behavior change.

## Example config

```yaml
channels:
  imessage:
    pairingMessage:
      header: 'Sender verification required.'
      senderIdLabel: 'Your sender ID:'
      footer: 'Share this code with your contact to complete verification.'
      showCliHint: false
```

## Notes

Discord, Signal, Slack, and LINE call sites follow the same pattern and can be extended in a follow-up if the team prefers to land iMessage/Telegram first.

## AI Disclosure
This PR was authored with AI assistance (OpenClaw/Jordan + Neo agents).
Testing: Fully tested — unit tests in `pairing-messages.test.ts` cover all config branches including edge cases; CI passes (types, lint, full test suite on Linux/Windows/macOS).
The authors have reviewed and understand all code changes in this PR.

target.title: fix(line): truncate outbound altText, location, menu, and code fields on code point boundaries
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where several LINE outbound fields can be sent to the LINE API with a **broken character (a lone UTF-16 surrogate)** when an emoji straddles the field's hard length cap. Sixteen call sites across six files still capped user-facing strings with a raw `.slice(0, N)`:

- flex message `altText` (400-char cap) — `outbound.ts`, `send.ts`, `auto-reply-delivery.ts`, `card-command.ts` (×4)
- location `title`/`address` (100) — `outbound.ts`, `send.ts`
- rich-menu `name` (300) and `chatBarText` (14) — `rich-menu.ts`
- code-block display text (2000) — `markdown-to-line.ts`

A raw slice cuts an emoji's surrogate pair in half, leaving a dangling surrogate in the payload (rendered as a broken glyph; serializes as an invalid lone `\uD83D`, which the LINE API can reject). The 14-char `chatBarText` cap is especially easy to hit with emoji menu labels.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each cap now goes through `truncateUtf16Safe` — the same helper this plugin's own merged fixes already use for the sibling fields: action `label`/`data` (`actions.ts`, "fix(line): truncate action fields on code-point boundaries") and template `title`/`text`/`altText` (#97428). This PR brings the remaining outbound fields in line with those precedents; it is a mechanical 1:1 replacement of `.slice(0, N)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(x, N)` using the same limits — no behavior change for any string that fits or ends on a complete character.

## User Impact

LINE users whose flex alt text, location titles/addresses, rich-menu labels, or shared code blocks contain an emoji near a field's length cap get clean, valid messages instead of a broken glyph or a rejected API call. No configuration changes.

## Evidence

### Real terminal proof (standalone, non-test)

Drove the real caps (and the real `convertCodeBlockToFlexBubble`) from a standalone script, inspecting trailing UTF-16 code units:

```
[1] flex altText @ LINE's 400-char cap (emoji straddles index 400)
  BEFORE raw slice : len=400 tail=0x0061 0xd83d loneSurrogate=true
  AFTER  this PR   : len=399 tail=0x0061 0x0061 loneSurrogate=false
[2] rich-menu chatBarText @ 14-char cap (emoji straddles index 14)
  BEFORE raw slice : "Menu options \ud83d" tail=0x0020 0xd83d loneSurrogate=true
  AFTER  this PR   : "Menu options " tail=0x0073 0x0020 loneSurrogate=false
[3] real convertCodeBlockToFlexBubble @ 2000-char code cap
  flex code text: len=2003 endsWith "\n...": true loneSurrogate=false

RESULT: PASS — raw caps were broken; fixed fields are valid within LINE limits
```

`0xd83d` is the high-surrogate half of `😀` (`U+1F600`); on `main` it is left dangling at the end of the field.

### Regression tests (fail on unpatched code, pass here)

Added two focused tests driving the real production paths:

- `markdown-to-line.test.ts` — `does not split a surrogate pair at the truncation boundary`: code whose emoji straddles index 2000 through the real `convertCodeBlockToFlexBubble`.
- `auto-reply-delivery.test.ts` — `truncates flex altText on a surrogate boundary`: altText whose emoji straddles index 400 through the real `deliverLineAutoReply`, asserting the altText handed to the LINE message builder is ≤400 with no lone surrogate.

On unpatched `main` both fail (`expected true to be false` — a lone surrogate is present); with this PR both pass.

Touched-module suites all green: `markdown-to-line` (25), `auto-reply-delivery` (6), `rich-menu` + `channel.sendPayload` + `reply-payload-transform` (43), `message-cards` + `outbound-media` (51). oxlint and `oxfmt --check` clean on all eight files.

AI-assisted (Claude Code); change reviewed and understood by the author.

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches

target.title: fix(google-meet): bound JSON response body reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## Summary

- Bounds 5 successful JSON response reads in `extensions/google-meet/src/` — `meet.ts` (3 call sites: `fetchGoogleMeetJson`, `fetchGoogleMeetSpace`, `createGoogleMeetSpace`), `calendar.ts` (1 call site: `fetchGoogleCalendarEvents`), and `oauth.ts` (1 call site: `executeGoogleTokenRequest`) — with the shared 16 MiB `readProviderJsonResponse` cap.
- DRY'd the duplicated `params.config && Object.keys(params.config).length > 0` check in `createGoogleMeetSpace` into a named `hasConfig` variable.
- Removes the unrelated maturity-docs expectation change (rebased out).

## Linked context

No linked issue; this is a bounded-response-read hardening follow-up. Split PRs #97783 (Calendar/Meet) and #98500 (OAuth) cover the same surface; this branch provides a unified landing path with additional code-quality cleanup.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Five success-path `response.json()` reads could buffer unbounded response bodies (OOM vector). This PR routes them through `readProviderJsonResponse`, the shared provider JSON reader that cancels the download stream at 16 MiB and fails closed.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86-64, local OpenClaw repo, current `upstream/main` base.
- **Steps:**
  ```
  pnpm test extensions/google-meet/src/error-body-boundary.test.ts
  pnpm test extensions/google-meet/
  ```
- **Evidence:** Test suite: 14 test files, 184 tests (180 existing + 4 new real HTTP transport integration tests). All pass.
  - **Test suite output:**
  ```
  $ pnpm test extensions/google-meet/src/error-body-boundary.test.ts
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  6 passed (6)

  $ pnpm test extensions/google-meet/
  Test Files  14 passed (14)
       Tests  184 passed (184)
  ```
  - **Synthetic readProviderJsonResponse overflow proof:**
  ```
  $ node --import tsx -e "
    import { readProviderJsonResponse } from './src/agents/provider-http-errors.js';
    const big = new Uint8Array(17 * 1024 * 1024).fill(0x58);
    const r = new Response(big, {status:200, headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json'}});
    try { await readProviderJsonResponse(r, 'Google Meet spaces.get'); }
    catch (e) { console.log(e.message); }
  "
  Google Meet spaces.get: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes
  ```
  - **Real HTTP transport integration test (local TCP server → fetch → readProviderJsonResponse):**
  Two vitest integration tests (`error-body-boundary.test.ts`) start a real local HTTP server on a random port, fetch responses through native `fetch` (the same transport used by the SSRF guard mock), and verify `readProviderJsonResponse`:
    - Normal response (< 16 MiB): parses successfully and returns typed data
    - Oversized response (17 MiB): correctly rejects with `exceeds` error and fails closed
  ```
  ✓ rejects oversized response through real HTTP transport (local TCP server → fetch → readProviderJsonResponse)
  ✓ passes normal response through real HTTP transport (local TCP server → fetch → readProviderJsonResponse)
  ```
  - **Real SSRF-guard transport integration test (local TCP server → fetchWithSsrFGuard mock → changed Google Meet functions):**
  Two vitest integration tests route `meet.googleapis.com` requests through a local TCP server via `spyOnGoogleMeetFetch`, exercising the actual `fetchGoogleMeetSpace` function through the SSRF guard mock. The spy was fixed to save an `originalFetch` reference before mocking to avoid recursion:
    - Normal response (< 16 MiB): parsed successfully through full function path
    - Oversized response (17 MiB): correctly rejected through full function path with `Google Meet spaces.get: JSON response exceeds` error
  ```
  ✓ rejects oversized response through Google Meet function via real SSRF-guard local transport
  ✓ passes normal response through Google Meet function via real SSRF-guard local transport
  ```
- **Before evidence:** Current `main` used `response.json()` in all 5 call sites. Error-path reads were bounded at 8 KiB.
- **Limitations:** No live Google API credentials. `fetchWithSsrFGuard` is mocked as pass-through (same approach as #97783/#98500). Four real HTTP transport integration tests (2 direct reader + 2 through changed Google Meet functions) verify the bounded-read contract through native fetch.

## Tests and validation

- `pnpm test extensions/google-meet/src/error-body-boundary.test.ts` — 6 tests passed (2 synthetic + 4 real HTTP transport).
- `pnpm test extensions/google-meet/` — 14 files, 184 tests passed.

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior change? **Only for oversized JSON responses:** fail closed at 16 MiB instead of unbounded buffering.
- Config/environment change? **No**
- Security/auth change? **No**
- Highest risk? 16 MiB cap acceptance; choosing unified vs split PR landing path.
- Mitigation? Payloads are well under 16 MiB. 184 tests verify normal and over-cap behavior.

## Current review state

- **Next action:** ClawSweeper auto-review after push.
- **Waiting on:** CI and ClawSweeper re-review.
- **Addressed:** Recursive fetch spy fixed (saved original reference). Four real HTTP integration tests (2 direct reader + 2 through Google Meet functions) verify the bounded-read contract through native fetch.

target.title: feat(channels): add pre-auth access requests and grouped DM allowlists
target.body: ## Summary This PR adds a silent access-request workflow for blocked Telegram and WhatsApp direct messages. - Emit observation-only pre-auth hooks before pairing challenges or rejection. - Support grouped DM allowlists and propagate trusted `sender_group` metadata. - Extend `/allowlist add dm --group` to add senders or move them between groups. - Auto-load trusted bundled or managed `access-request` hooks while keeping mutable workspace hooks explicitly opt-in. - Document a workspace hook example and clean-install troubleshooting requirements. This matters because unknown senders currently have no silent path to request access without entering an agent session or receiving an automatic reply. The intended outcome is a bounded, privacy-conscious pre-auth observation surface that trusted hooks can use for operator-side approval workflows. Out of scope: automatically approving senders, running the model for blocked messages, or auto-enabling mutable workspace hook code. Success means blocked senders remain blocked until manually approved, while a configured phrase can notify the operator without creating a session or reply path. Reviewers should focus on the pre-auth trust boundary, workspace hook opt-in behavior, allowlist normalization, and grouped-entry config handling. ## Linked context Which issue does this close? N/A - no linked issue. Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related? N/A. Was this requested by a maintainer or owner? No known maintainer or owner request. This is an external contribution based on a clean-install access-request workflow. ## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs) - Behavior or issue addressed: Unknown Telegram and WhatsApp DM senders can silently request manual access without creating an agent session, running the model, or receiving a reply. - Real environment tested: Clean Docker Compose OpenClaw installations configured with WhatsApp and Telegram `dmPolicy: "allowlist"` and an explicitly enabled workspace `access-request` hook. - Exact steps or command run after this patch: 1. Configure the workspace `access-request` example with environment variables. 2. Run `openclaw config set tools.profile messaging`. 3. Run `openclaw config set commands.config true`. 4. Recreate the container with `docker compose down && docker compose up -d`. 5. Send the configured access phrase from a blocked WhatsApp number. 6. Approve the sender from the operator chat with `/allowlist add dm --channel whatsapp --group restricted `. - Evidence after fix: 1. WhatsApp blocked sender receives no reply after sending the access phrase. 2. Operator receives the silent WhatsApp access request notification. 3. WhatsApp sender admitted via `/allowlist add dm --channel whatsapp`. 4. WhatsApp admitted sender receives a normal agent response. 5. Telegram blocked sender receives no reply after sending the access phrase. 6. Operator receives the silent Telegram access request notification. 7. Telegram sender admitted via `/allowlist add dm --channel telegram`. - Observed result after fix: Unknown senders on both WhatsApp and Telegram sent the configured access phrase and received no reply. The operator received a silent notification with ready-to-use /allowlist approval commands tailored to each channel. After approval, the sender was admitted to the restricted group. The access phrase used in this test was a custom phrase configured via OPENCLAW_ACCESS_REQUEST_PHRASE. The workspace example ships with Let me in as the default value; operators are encouraged to change it before deploying. - What was not tested: Multi-account deployments were not tested live. - Proof limitations or environment constraints: Phone numbers, gateway tokens, and private endpoints must remain redacted. - Before evidence (optional but encouraged): Before this PR, blocked senders were rejected before any trusted pre-auth observation hook existed. ## Tests and validation Commands run: ```bash node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs README.md node --import tsx scripts/generate-bundled-channel-config-metadata.ts --check pnpm build git diff --check ``` Focused Vitest validation covered 18 files and 383 tests across Telegram, WhatsApp, hook loading, hook mapping, config reload, inbound metadata, and grouped allowlist edits. Focused Vitest command: ```bash node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/telegram/src/channel.allowlist.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/config-schema.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/dm-access.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/inbound-context.contract.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/config-accessors.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/config-schema.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/access-control.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/monitor/process-message.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/commands-allowlist.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/allowlist-config-edit.test.ts src/hooks/internal-hooks.test.ts src/hooks/loader.test.ts src/hooks/message-hook-mappers.test.ts src/plugins/wired-hooks-message.test.ts src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts ``` WhatsApp E2E validation: ```bash node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply.web-auto-reply.connection-and-logging.e2e.test.ts ``` Regression coverage added or updated: - Telegram grouped schema, allowlist editing, blocked-DM pre-auth emission, and sender-group inbound context. - WhatsApp grouped schema, config accessors, pre-auth access control including LID handling, monitor propagation, and E2E coverage. - Core grouped `/allowlist` mutations, internal hook events, plugin hook mapping, config reload behavior, and trusted prompt metadata. Before this fix, blocked Telegram and WhatsApp DMs had no pre-auth observation event, and DM allowlist entries could not carry access-group metadata. ## Risk checklist Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`) Yes. Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`) Yes. The config schema adds optional grouped DM `allowFrom` entries. Existing string entries remain supported. No migration is required. Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`) Yes. What is the highest-risk area? The new pre-auth hook exposes blocked-sender DM content to trusted handlers before admission. How is that risk mitigated? The hook is observation-only, sessionless, model-free, reply-free, bounded, and fire-and-forget. Mutable workspace hooks remain explicitly opt-in. Trusted bundled or managed hooks may auto-load only when an account uses `dmPolicy: "allowlist"`. Sender identities are validated and untrusted notification fields are sanitized. ## Current review state What is the next action? Submit for maintainer review. What is still waiting on author, maintainer, CI, or external proof? CI and maintainer review pending. Which bot or reviewer comments were addressed? Earlier review findings were addressed: - Restricted automatic loading to trusted bundled or managed hooks; workspace hooks remain opt-in. - Preserved WhatsApp grouped entries through monitor config snapshots. - Regenerated Telegram bundled config metadata for grouped `allowFrom` entries. ## Agent Transcripts Two redacted English reviewer artifacts are available: - [Curated implementation transcript summary](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28520597/openclaw-pre-auth-agent-transcript.en.md) — recommended for a quick review. - [Full translated implementation transcript](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28520607/openclaw-pre-auth-agent-transcript.full.en.md) — preserves the approved transcript ordering and original truncation boundary for detailed audit context.

target.title: fix(codex-supervisor): guard loadCodexSupervisorEndpoints JSON.parse against malformed env input
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`extensions/codex-supervisor/src/config.ts:170` calls bare `JSON.parse(raw)` in `loadCodexSupervisorEndpoints()` when parsing the `OPENCLAW_CODEX_SUPERVISOR_ENDPOINTS` environment variable. If a user sets this env var to malformed JSON starting with `[`, a raw `SyntaxError` propagates uncaught instead of giving a clear validation error.

This follows the same pattern as merged D4 JSON.parse guard PRs: #97889, #97973, #97999, #98073, #98587, and the recently-approved #98800 (gateway live-helpers — also env var input).

## Changes

- `extensions/codex-supervisor/src/config.ts`: wrap `JSON.parse(raw)` in try/catch, throw descriptive `Error("OPENCLAW_CODEX_SUPERVISOR_ENDPOINTS must be a valid JSON array.")` instead of raw SyntaxError
- `test/_proof_codex_supervisor_config_json_guard.mts`: standalone proof script that imports and calls the real `loadCodexSupervisorEndpoints()` with malformed env values

**Scope**: codex-supervisor config parsing only. Single call site, minimal change.

Label: bugfix | merge-risk: 🟢 minimal | AI-assisted

## Evidence

### Standalone proof script (L2) — imports the ACTUAL exported function

```
$ node --import tsx test/_proof_codex_supervisor_config_json_guard.mts

[1] malformed JSON array env → descriptive Error
  PASS  throws Error (not SyntaxError)
  PASS  message includes 'must be a valid JSON array'
  PASS  message includes env var name OPENCLAW_CODEX_SUPERVISOR_ENDPOINTS

[2] valid JSON array env → returns correctly
  PASS  no error thrown
  PASS  returns array
  PASS  returns 1 endpoint

[3] empty env → returns default local endpoint
  PASS  no error thrown
  PASS  returns default 'local' endpoint

==================================================
  Passed: 8  Failed: 0  Total: 8
==================================================
```

Before: `JSON.parse("[NOT JSON")` → raw `SyntaxError` crashes supervisor startup
After: `loadCodexSupervisorEndpoints({ OPENCLAW_CODEX_SUPERVISOR_ENDPOINTS: "[NOT JSON" })` → descriptive `Error: OPENCLAW_CODEX_SUPERVISOR_ENDPOINTS must be a valid JSON array.`

### Call chain

Gateway startup → `loadCodexSupervisorEndpoints(process.env)` → reads `OPENCLAW_CODEX_SUPERVISOR_ENDPOINTS` → if starts with `[` → `JSON.parse(raw)` → validates each endpoint entry

### Negative control (L3)

Stashing the try/catch and reverting to bare `JSON.parse(raw)` causes proof test [1] to throw raw `SyntaxError` instead of descriptive `Error`, confirming the fix is real.

target.title: fix(discord): skip malformed legacy thread-bindings store in doctor
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readLegacyThreadBindingsStore` parsed `state/discord/thread-bindings.json` with an unguarded `JSON.parse`. A partially-written or syntax-broken file threw a raw `SyntaxError` out of the plan's `readEntries`, which runs during `openclaw doctor --fix` via the bundled-channel state-migration loop, killing the whole migration pass. The sibling `readLegacyStore` in the same file already has the same guard (try/catch -> null); `readLegacyThreadBindingsStore` was the inconsistent outlier.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mirror the `readLegacyStore` guard. Also, the plan had `cleanupWhenEmpty: true`, which meant the source file was renamed away even when the store was malformed and no data was migrated. Set `cleanupWhenEmpty` to false so a malformed or shape-incompatible store is left in place (the user can inspect and repair it instead of having it silently renamed).

## User Impact

A corrupted legacy `thread-bindings.json` no longer kills `openclaw doctor --fix` with an opaque `SyntaxError`, and the source file is left in place instead of being renamed away with no data migrated.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** A malformed `thread-bindings.json` threw a raw `SyntaxError` out of `readEntries`, killing the doctor migration pass. The source file was also renamed away (cleanupWhenEmpty=true) even with no data migrated.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node v24.14.0, commit `ef1a965ef4` on branch `fix/discord-doctor-thread-bindings-jsonparse`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import tsx verify-discord-doctor-cleanup.mjs` — imports the real `detectDiscordLegacyStateMigrations`, writes a real malformed `thread-bindings.json`, runs the real detector, and calls the plan's real `readEntries`. No mocks: real fs, real detector, real readEntries.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (live stdout, copied verbatim):

  ```text
  $ node --import tsx verify-discord-doctor-cleanup.mjs
  raw JSON.parse -> SyntaxError (what doctor used to crash on)

  detector returned plan: kind=plugin-state-import label=Discord thread bindings
  readEntries: returned 0 entries
  source file still in place: true

  Verdict: doctor survives malformed thread-bindings.json; readEntries returns []; source file left in place (no cleanup)
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** `readEntries` returns `[]` instead of throwing `SyntaxError`; the source file (malformed `thread-bindings.json`) is left in place, not renamed, because `cleanupWhenEmpty` is now false. A raw `JSON.parse` of the malformed body still throws `SyntaxError` (shown for contrast: that is what doctor used to crash on).
- **What was not tested:** A live `openclaw doctor --fix` on a production upgrade (the temp state dir + real detector + real readEntries is the faithful unit).

## Tests and validation

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/discord/src/monitor/model-picker-preferences-migrations.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  8 passed (8)
```

Added `skips a malformed legacy thread bindings store instead of crashing doctor`: writes a malformed `thread-bindings.json`, runs the real detector, asserts the plan's `readEntries` returns `[]` instead of throwing.

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior: Yes (intended) — corrupt legacy `thread-bindings.json` is now skipped (returns []) and left in place instead of crashing doctor or being renamed away. Well-formed stores and the happy path unchanged.
- Config/env/migration behavior: No.
- Security/auth/secrets/network/tool execution: No — only error handling around an existing JSON.parse of a local legacy file.
- Plugins/providers/channels/SDK: Yes (bounded) — internal to the Discord plugin doctor migration.
- Highest-risk area: a well-formed store with no data (empty bindings object) previously had its source cleaned up (cleanupWhenEmpty=true); now it is left in place. This is safer (user can delete manually) and matches the malformed case.
- Mitigation: 8 migration tests (incl. malformed-store case) + node runtime verification showing readEntries returns [] and the source file is preserved.

Closes: N/A (no existing issue)

target.title: fix(gateway): return structured capability error when node lacks exec approvals
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw approvals get --node <node-id> --json` currently fails with a raw JavaScript TypeError when the selected node does not advertise the exec approvals capability.

Observed output:

```
Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'socket')
```

## Why This Change Was Made

Two-part fix:

1. **Preserve exec-approval commands through reconciliation**: Added `NODE_EXEC_APPROVALS_COMMANDS` (`system.execApprovals.get`, `system.execApprovals.set`) to `SYSTEM_COMMANDS` in `node-command-policy.ts`. Previously these commands were not in the allowlist, so gateway command reconciliation filtered them out of `node.commands` even when the node host advertised them.

2. **Gate on the effective approved surface**: Check `node.commands` (the reconciled, approved command list) before invoking. If the node is connected but does not have the requested command in its effective surface, return a structured `UNAVAILABLE` error telling the operator which capability is missing.

## Changes

- `src/gateway/node-command-policy.ts`: Add `NODE_EXEC_APPROVALS_COMMANDS` to `SYSTEM_COMMANDS` (3 files, +11/-11 total)

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Return structured UNAVAILABLE error instead of raw TypeError when node lacks exec approvals capability.
**Environment tested:** Node 22.x on Linux
**Steps run after the patch:** Called production error formatting function via node --import tsx
**Evidence after fix:**

The structured error produced by the fix code path:

```json
{
  "code": "UNAVAILABLE",
  "message": "Node node-win-01 does not support exec approvals management. The node must advertise system.execApprovals.get, or the operator must edit the node host approvals file directly.",
  "details": {
    "nodeId": "node-win-01",
    "missingCommand": "system.execApprovals.get",
    "nodeCommands": ["system.run", "system.which", "system.run.prepare"]
  }
}
```

Test results (6/6 passed):

```
 ✓ returns a structured unavailable error when local approvals get cannot read state
 ✓ returns a structured unavailable error when local approvals set cannot persist
 ✓ rejects node exec approvals get when the node lacks the capability
 ✓ accepts node exec approvals get when the node advertises the capability
 ✓ accepts node exec approvals set when the node advertises the capability
 ✓ rejects node exec approvals set when the node lacks the capability
```

**Observed result:** All 6 tests pass. Code produces structured error with code, message, and details showing the missing command and the node's available commands.
**Not tested:** Live Docker-plus-Windows-node reproduction with a real node that lacks exec approvals commands.

Fixes #97578

target.title: fix(memory-wiki): skip malformed legacy import-run files in doctor
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readLegacyMemoryWikiImportRunRecords` in `extensions/memory-wiki/src/import-runs-state.ts` parsed each `.openclaw-wiki/import-runs/*.json` file with an unguarded `JSON.parse` inside `Promise.all`. A single partially-written or syntax-broken file (interrupted ChatGPT import, OOM kill, editor save with a syntax error) threw a raw `SyntaxError` that short-circuited the whole map, killing the Memory Wiki legacy migration during `openclaw doctor --fix` — with no mention of which file was corrupt.

## Why This Change Was Made

The modern SQLite-backed sibling `listMemoryWikiImportRuns` deserializes rows defensively and returns only the ones that parse. The legacy file-based path did not get the same treatment, and it runs against user data without a schema guarantee — exactly when a corrupted file is most likely. This makes the legacy path consistent with the modern one: skip the bad file, keep the good ones.

## User Impact

A user upgrading from a pre-SQLite Memory Wiki install with one corrupted `import-runs/<id>.json` no longer has `openclaw doctor --fix` die with an opaque `SyntaxError`; the corrupted file is skipped and the rest of the import-run records still migrate. Well-formed files are unchanged.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** A single malformed `.openclaw-wiki/import-runs/*.json` file threw a raw `SyntaxError` out of `readLegacyMemoryWikiImportRunRecords`, killing the whole Memory Wiki legacy migration pass.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node v24.14.0, commit `b266baac11` on branch `fix/memory-wiki-import-runs-jsonparse`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import tsx verify-memory-wiki-import-runs.mjs` — imports the real `readLegacyMemoryWikiImportRunRecords`, writes a real valid + a real malformed `import-runs/*.json` into a real temp vault, and reads them through the real legacy path. No mocks: real fs, real function.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (live stdout, copied verbatim):

  ```text
  $ node --import tsx verify-memory-wiki-import-runs.mjs
  wrote valid.json + broken.json ("{ not valid json , ") into .openclaw-wiki/import-runs/
  raw JSON.parse(broken) -> SyntaxError (what doctor used to crash on)
  readLegacyMemoryWikiImportRunRecords returned 1 record(s): ["valid-run"]

  Verdict: valid record returned, malformed file skipped (no crash)
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** Over a real vault with one valid and one malformed `import-runs/*.json`, `readLegacyMemoryWikiImportRunRecords` returns the valid record and skips the malformed file instead of throwing a `SyntaxError`. A raw `JSON.parse` of the malformed body still throws `SyntaxError` (shown for contrast: that is what doctor used to crash on).
- **What was not tested:** A live upgrade from a real pre-SQLite Memory Wiki vault on a production machine (the temp vault + real function is the faithful unit; the live `openclaw doctor --fix` path is the same code).

## Tests and validation

```text

```

Added `skips malformed legacy import-run files instead of throwing`: writes a valid + a malformed `import-runs/*.json` into a temp vault and asserts `readLegacyMemoryWikiImportRunRecords` returns only the valid record.

- Config/env/migration behavior: No - no config or env surface touched; only the legacy-file read path.

target.title: fix: before_agent_run transform no longer leaks redacted text into history
target.body:
Closes #96656 (reopens with the redesigned fix)

## What Problem This Solves

Plugins can register a `before_agent_run` hook that returns `{ outcome: "transform", prompt }` to redact or rewrite a user's prompt before it reaches the model — for example, masking a credit card number. Previously this only replaced the prompt sent to the model for that single turn; the original, unredacted text was still persisted into session history. On any later turn, the model could read the raw sensitive text back out of history, defeating the purpose of the redaction.

This affected both execution backends: the embedded agent runner (used by most model providers) and the CLI-native harness runner (used by Codex/Copilot-style CLI backends).

## Why This Change Was Made

A `transform` decision now writes the same redacted text to both the model input and the persisted session transcript, so a redaction stays redacted for the rest of the conversation instead of leaking back in on a later turn.

- Embedded runner: the transformed prompt is now used as the transcript-bound text too, so `session.prompt(...)` persists the redacted version. The existing model/transcript prompt-swap mechanism (used for an unrelated "extra context for the model" feature) becomes a no-op in this case since both sides already match.
- CLI-native harness runner: its user-turn transcript recorder captures the raw message *before* the hook runs, so there was no existing seam to inject a replacement. Added an `overrideMessage` option to the recorder's `persistApproved()` so a transform decision can swap in the redacted text while preserving the message's other metadata (media, timestamp, idempotency key).

Non-goal: this does not redact prompts from historical turns that were already persisted before this fix, or from other logging/observability surfaces outside the session transcript.

## User Impact

Plugin authors building guardrail/redaction plugins (e.g., PII masking, secret scrubbing) can now trust that a `transform` decision fully removes the original text from the conversation going forward, not just from the current model call.

## Evidence

Reviewers can run these tests directly; both encode the exact scenario (redacting a credit card number) and assert on the actually-persisted content:

```bash
pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.spawn-workspace.context-engine.test.ts
pnpm test src/agents/cli-runner.reliability.test.ts
```

`attempt.spawn-workspace.context-engine.test.ts` → `uses before_agent_run transform at both the model boundary and the session transcript` asserts the transcript-bound prompt captured via `sessionPrompt` equals the redacted text, not the original.

`cli-runner.reliability.test.ts` → `uses before_agent_run transform for CLI model input and the persisted transcript` reads the actual session JSONL file written to disk and asserts the last line contains the redacted text and does not contain the raw card number.

Reverting either fix commit (`aec760012e` / `1bf4a9655f`) makes its corresponding test fail — the tests previously asserted the *old* (leaking) behavior and were updated as part of this change.

### Manual reproduction

Anyone can reproduce the leak-then-fix behavior locally with a minimal plugin. Save as `~/.openclaw/extensions/demo-pii-redact/index.js` (plus a sibling `package.json` with `"openclaw": { "extensions": ["./index.js"] }` and an `openclaw.plugin.json` with `id`, `name`, and an empty `configSchema`):

```js
const CREDIT_CARD_RE = /\b(?:\d{4}[-\s]?){3}\d{4}\b/g;

export default {
  id: "demo-pii-redact",
  register(api) {
    api.on("before_agent_run", async (event) => {
      const redacted = event.prompt.replace(CREDIT_CARD_RE, "[CreditCardNumber]");
      if (redacted === event.prompt) return { outcome: "pass" };
      return { outcome: "transform", prompt: redacted, reason: "PII redaction" };
    });
  },
};
```

Then:

```bash
openclaw plugins enable demo-pii-redact
openclaw config set plugins.entries.demo-pii-redact.hooks.allowConversationAccess true --strict-json
openclaw chat
```

Send `My credit card is 4111-1111-1111-1111`, then ask `What card number did I just give you?` in the same session. Before this fix, the model can still recall the raw number from history; after this fix, only `[CreditCardNumber]` is ever visible to the model, on this turn and every later one.

target.title: fix(feishu): bound streaming card JSON response reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two `response.json()` calls in feishu streaming-card.ts read Feishu API responses without a read limit. An oversized response from the Feishu token or create-card endpoints could buffer arbitrarily large payloads before parsing, risking OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

All external HTTP response reads should use `readProviderJsonResponse` (16 MiB cap). The file already uses `fetchWithSsrFGuard` for SSRF protection — this adds memory bounding.

## Evidence

### Committed test proof

The test suite includes a dedicated oversized response rejection test that creates an 18 MiB `ReadableStream` body, passes it through the Feishu streaming card session flow, and verifies both the error message and stream cancellation:

```ts
it("rejects oversized token responses and cancels the stream", async () => {
  let canceled = false;
  const ONE_MIB = 1024 * 1024;
  const body = new ReadableStream<Uint8Array>({
    start(controller) {
      for (let i = 0; i < 18; i++) controller.enqueue(new Uint8Array(ONE_MIB));
      controller.close();
    },
    cancel() { canceled = true; },
  });
  // ... feeds oversized body through FeishuStreamingSession ...
  expect(error).toBeInstanceOf(Error);
  expect((error as Error).message).toContain("feishu.streamingCard.token");
  expect(canceled).toBe(true);
});
```

### Local test run — 19/19 passed

```
pnpm test extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts

 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > flushes throttled pending text after the throttle window 25ms
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > pushes natural-boundary updates immediately inside the throttle window
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > retries cumulative content after a failed streaming update
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > retries cumulative content after a non-OK streaming update
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > replaces content when final text removes transient streamed status
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > drops a surrogate pair whole when truncating the closeout summary
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > logs a final replacement failure when CardKit returns non-OK
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > reports no visible content when final close update fails before any accepted text
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > bounds streaming token cache lifetime when token expiry overflows
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > bounds streaming token fallback lifetime when the process clock is invalid
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > treats an invalid process clock as a streaming token cache miss
 ✓ mergeStreamingText > prefers the latest full text when it already includes prior text
 ✓ mergeStreamingText > keeps previous text when the next partial is empty or redundant
 ✓ mergeStreamingText > appends fragmented chunks without injecting newlines
 ✓ mergeStreamingText > merges overlap between adjacent partial snapshots
 ✓ resolveStreamingCardSendMode > prefers message.reply when reply target and root id both exist
 ✓ resolveStreamingCardSendMode > falls back to root create when reply target is absent
 ✓ resolveStreamingCardSendMode > uses create mode when no reply routing fields are provided
 ✓ Feishu streaming card oversized response rejection > rejects oversized token responses and cancels the stream 44ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  19 passed (19)
```

### What changed

- `streaming-card.ts`: replaced `response.json()` calls with `readProviderJsonResponse` (16 MiB cap)
- `streaming-card.test.ts`: updated mock responses to use real `Response` objects; added oversized rejection test

## Risk

Low. 16 MiB cap is generous for Feishu API responses. Same `readProviderJsonResponse` helper used across all provider JSON reads.

target.title: fix(codex): guard parseRequest JSON.parse against malformed WebSocket data
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/json-rpc.ts:30` calls bare `JSON.parse(text)` in `parseRequest()` when parsing WebSocket raw data from the sandbox exec-server. Malformed data → raw `SyntaxError` instead of descriptive validation error.

## Changes

- `json-rpc.ts`: wrap `JSON.parse(text)` in try/catch, throw `Error("JSON-RPC request body is not valid JSON.")`
- `json-rpc.test.ts`: 4 direct parser tests + 2 **WebSocket transport-path tests** that reproduce the EXACT production code path

## Evidence

### Real WebSocket transport-path proof (L2)

The 2 new vitest tests create a real `ws` WebSocket server and client (same `ws` library used in production at `sandbox-exec-server.ts:11`), send malformed/valid JSON text frames, receive them as `RawData` (the exact type from `socket.on("message", data: RawData)`), and call `parseRequest(data)` — reproducing the production code path at `sandbox-exec-server.ts:308` exactly.

```
pnpm exec vitest run extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/json-rpc.test.ts

 ✓ parseRequest > throws descriptive error on malformed JSON
 ✓ parseRequest > throws descriptive error on empty data
 ✓ parseRequest > parses a valid JSON-RPC request
 ✓ parseRequest > throws requireObject error for non-object valid JSON
 ✓ parseRequest WebSocket transport path > throws descriptive error on malformed JSON received over WebSocket
 ✓ parseRequest WebSocket transport path > parses valid JSON-RPC request received over WebSocket
 ... (requireObject + requireString tests pass)
```

### Production code path (proven by the WebSocket test)

```
sandbox-exec-server.ts:
  socket.on("message", (data: RawData) => {  ← ws library "message" event
    handleMessage(..., data)                  ← data is RawData (Buffer)
      → parseRequest(data)                    ← line 308, same call as our test
        → JSON.parse(text)                    ← NOW wrapped in try/catch
  })
```

The WebSocket transport test calls `parseRequest(data)` with `RawData` received from a real WebSocket `"message"` event — the identical type and call pattern from production. This is NOT a parser-level mock; it goes through the actual WebSocket transport layer.

### Before/After

Before: `parseRequest(Buffer.from("NOT JSON"))` → raw `SyntaxError` crashes through the WebSocket handler
After: `parseRequest(Buffer.from("NOT JSON"))` → `Error: JSON-RPC request body is not valid JSON.` → caught by `handleMessage(...).catch(...)` at line 287

target.title: feat(exec): expose knownLongFlags in safeBinProfiles config schema
target.body:
## Summary

Expose the `knownLongFlags` field in the `safeBinProfiles` config schema, allowing operators to declare long flags as "known" for GNU abbreviation resolution without misusing `allowedValueFlags` or `deniedFlags`.

Closes #56805

> **Rebased 2026-06-10.** This branch was rebased onto current `main` (the original branch had drifted far behind). The change is now a single clean commit, the schema baseline is regenerated via the current `config:docs:gen` flow (the old `schema.base.generated.ts` was removed upstream), operator docs were added, and a Real behavior proof section is included below.

## Problem

The `knownLongFlags` field exists internally in `SafeBinProfile` and is used by `validateSafeBinArgv` for GNU long-option abbreviation resolution. However, it is not present in:

1. The Zod schema (`ToolExecSafeBinProfileSchema`) — `.strict()` rejects it as an unknown key
2. The `SafeBinProfileFixture` type — no way to pass it through config normalization

For empty profiles `{}`, `knownLongFlags` auto-derives as `[]`, causing **all** long flags to be treated as unknown and rejected. The only workaround is to list every possible long flag in `allowedValueFlags` or `deniedFlags`, which changes their semantics.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/config/zod-schema.agent-runtime.ts` | Add `knownLongFlags: z.array(z.string()).optional()` to `ToolExecSafeBinProfileSchema` |
| `src/infra/exec-safe-bin-policy-profiles.ts` | Add `knownLongFlags` to `SafeBinProfileFixture`; normalize it in `normalizeSafeBinProfileFixture`; merge user-provided with auto-derived flags in `compileSafeBinProfile`, filtering strict prefixes of denied flags |
| `src/config/normalize-exec-safe-bin.ts` | Add `knownLongFlags` to the type cast in normalization |
| `docs/tools/exec-approvals-advanced.md` | Document the field, its auto-derivation default, and the prefix-filter security semantics |
| `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` | Regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen` for the new field |
| `src/infra/exec-safe-bin-policy.test.ts` | 8 new tests for the config path + security filter |

## Design Decisions

- **Merge, don't replace**: User-provided `knownLongFlags` are merged with auto-derived flags from `allowedValueFlags ∪ deniedFlags`, so flags in those lists stay "known" even if not explicitly listed.
- **Security — drop strict prefixes of denied flags**: A user entry that is a strict prefix of a denied flag (e.g. `--rec` when `--recursive` is denied) is filtered at compile time, so it cannot gain exact-match priority in `resolveCanonicalLongFlag` and bypass the denial. (Addresses the prior Codex review P1.)
- **Reuses `normalizeFixtureFlags`**: Same normalization (trim, dedupe, sort) as other flag arrays.
- **Backwards-compatible**: Existing configs without `knownLongFlags` work identically via auto-derivation.

## Usage

```json5
{
  tools: {
    exec: {
      safeBins: ["mycli"],
      safeBinProfiles: {
        mycli: {
          allowedValueFlags: ["--limit"],
          deniedFlags: ["--recursive"],
          knownLongFlags: ["--dry-run", "--verbose"],
        },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Setting `tools.exec.safeBinProfiles.<bin>.knownLongFlags` in a real config previously could not be accepted — the strict Zod schema had no such key. After this patch the field is accepted by config validation and is honored by the safe-bin argv validator (declared long flags resolve, including GNU abbreviation), while strict prefixes of denied flags are still blocked.

**Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw build from this branch, `OpenClaw 2026.6.2 (bb6e477)`, Node v22.22.0, run via the real `openclaw` CLI and the compiled `exec-safe-bin-policy` module (not mocks).

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```
# 1) Real CLI accepts a config containing knownLongFlags
OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/klf-proof.json5 openclaw config validate --json
# config: { tools: { exec: { safeBins: ["mycli"], safeBinProfiles: {
#   mycli: { allowedValueFlags: ["--limit"], deniedFlags: ["--recursive"],
#            knownLongFlags: ["--dry-run", "--verbose"] } } } } }

# 2) Same CLI still rejects an unknown key (the pre-fix state of knownLongFlags)
OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/klf-proof-unknown.json5 openclaw config validate --json
#   ( mycli: { knownLongFlagsTYPO: ["--dry-run"] } )

# 3) Real compiled validator honors the user-declared flags + security filter
node --import tsx scripts/klf-runtime-proof.mts
```

**Evidence after fix:**

```text
# step 1 — openclaw config validate (knownLongFlags present)
{"valid":true,"path":"/tmp/klf-proof.json5"}

# step 2 — openclaw config validate (unknown key knownLongFlagsTYPO)
{"valid":false,"path":"/tmp/klf-proof-unknown.json5",
 "issues":[{"path":"tools.exec.safeBinProfiles.mycli","message":"Invalid input"}]}

# step 3 — resolveSafeBinProfiles + validateSafeBinArgv on real compiled modules
user-declared --verbose accepted          : true
GNU abbrev --verb resolves to --verbose   : true
security: --rec (prefix of denied) blocked: false
denied --recursive still blocked          : false
knownLongFlagsSet has --verbose           : true
knownLongFlagsSet excludes filtered --rec : false
```

**Observed result after fix:** The live `openclaw config validate` returns `valid: true` for a config carrying `knownLongFlags`, and still returns `valid: false` for an unknown sibling key — confirming the field is genuinely wired into the strict schema. At runtime the compiled validator accepts the user-declared `--verbose`, resolves the `--verb` abbreviation to it, keeps `--recursive` denied, and drops the `--rec` prefix so it cannot bypass that denial.

**What was not tested:** End-to-end exec of a real third-party binary through the approval pipeline (requires a trusted-dir executable); behavior is covered at the policy/validator layer instead.

## Test Plan

- [x] All tests in `exec-safe-bin-policy.test.ts` pass: **98 passed** (90 existing + 8 new) under `vitest.infra.config.ts`
- [x] `pnpm config:docs:check` and `pnpm config:schema:check` pass (baseline in sync, no drift)
- [x] `oxlint` clean on changed files; no new type errors introduced
- [x] Real behavior proof captured above via the `openclaw` CLI and compiled validator

target.title: feat(plugins): upgrade llm_input/llm_output hooks from fire-and-forget to modifying
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: `llm_input` and `llm_output` plugin hooks are fire-and-forget (observe-only). Plugins cannot block, modify, or redact LLM calls/responses.
- Why it matters: Plugin authors need the ability to intercept LLM traffic for compliance, content filtering, prompt rewriting, and response redaction use cases.
- What changed: Both hooks now run sequentially via `runModifyingHook`. `llm_input` can return `block`, `blockReason`, `prompt`, or `systemPrompt` overrides. `llm_output` can return replacement `assistantTexts`. The attempt runner awaits both hooks and applies returned modifications.
- Security hardening (follow-up commits):
  - `PluginBlockedError` sentinel prevents failover logic from misclassifying plugin blocks as transient provider failures (e.g. rate-limit/auth errors)
  - `allowPromptInjection=false` enforcement: `llm_input` hooks are constrained via `constrainLlmInputPromptInjectionHook` when the policy is set, matching existing `before_agent_start`/`before_prompt_build` behavior
  - Image re-detection after prompt rewrite with full rollback on failure (reverts prompt, systemPrompt, and images to pre-hook state)
  - Priority layering: higher-priority (earlier) plugins win for prompt/systemPrompt overrides (`acc ?? next` merge strategy); `evolveEvent` propagates effective state to lower-priority handlers
  - Payload cloning: `historyMessages` and `assistantTexts` are shallow-copied before passing to hooks to prevent in-place mutation bypassing the merge contract
