target.title: test(gateway): clear dangling intervals in close, runtime-services, and startup-post-attach tests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three gateway test files create `setInterval` handles as mock dependencies but never clean them up:

- `src/gateway/server-close.test.ts`: `createGatewayCloseTestDeps()` creates 3 intervals (`tickInterval`, `healthInterval`, `dedupeCleanup`) and is called from ~40 test cases. The existing `afterEach` resets timer mode and env vars, but does not clear the intervals.
- `src/gateway/server-runtime-services.test.ts`: `createMaintenanceHandles()` creates 4 intervals. Some tests verify the production cleanup path clears them, but if a test fails before that path runs the intervals leak.
- `src/gateway/server-startup-post-attach.test.ts`: one test inline-creates 3 `setInterval(() => {}, 1 << 30)` handles with no cleanup.

Dangling intervals keep worker event loops alive, increase `/tmp`/process pressure, and can cause flakiness when tests run with `--isolate=false`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a consistent `trackTestInterval` helper in each file that records every `setInterval` handle created by test helpers, and clears them in `afterEach`. This mirrors the existing `test/helpers/temp-dir.ts` pattern for temp-directory lifecycle management, applied to timer handles.

Changes per file:

- `server-close.test.ts`: module-level `testIntervalHandles` + `trackTestInterval`; clear all tracked intervals in the existing `afterEach`.
- `server-runtime-services.test.ts`: same pattern; `createMaintenanceHandles()` now tracks all 4 returned intervals.
- `server-startup-post-attach.test.ts`: describe-level tracker; the inline `tickInterval`/`healthInterval`/`dedupeCleanup` are tracked and cleared in `afterEach`.

No production code is changed.

## User Impact

Test-only. Reduces dangling interval leaks during gateway test runs. No user-visible behavior change.

## Evidence

target.title: [codex] Fail closed pair slash command routing
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #98239.

The Control UI sends chat text literally through `chat.send`. A spaced plugin slash command such as `/ pair qr` did not match the active `/pair` registration, so it could continue through the normal agent path. In the reported Tailscale Serve setup, that exposed an availability risk because an agent turn could try to repair configuration and move `gateway.bind` away from the loopback backend used by Serve.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps the fix at the registered plugin-command boundary:

- the canonical plugin matcher accepts whitespace after `/`, including `/ pair qr`
- authorization probing recognizes spaced syntax only when the command is present in the active runtime registry
- mention-prefixed group text receives the same authorization treatment as canonical inline slash commands
- inactive or denied plugins do not reserve aliases
- plugin-before-built-in ordering, built-in reservations, command scopes, channel restrictions, and transport-neutral dispatch remain unchanged

The earlier manifest-level unavailable-handler fallback was removed because it would have established a new fail-closed policy for every manifest-declared runtime slash alias. This PR does not make that product-policy change.

## User Impact

When device-pair is active, `/ pair qr` is handled by the same authorized, LLM-free device-pair path as `/pair qr`; it cannot fall through into an agent turn. If device-pair is inactive or denied, the text keeps the existing inactive-plugin behavior rather than claiming a new command reservation.

## Evidence

Exact candidate: `bcfa481fbefb8895421d280cb977f71848d8d808`.

target.title: fix: Codex catalog honors app-server context caps
target.body:
Related: #93764

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running the Codex harness could see OpenClaw model context display and budgeting based on stale local context metadata when Codex app-server has a smaller native effective context window.

This is the OpenClaw consumer side of the fix. It consumes Codex app-server context metadata when the app-server exposes it; older Codex app-server builds keep the existing fallback catalog behavior.

Companion Codex branch: https://github.com/hannesrudolph/codex/tree/codex-model-context-metadata

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenClaw already has separate `contextWindow` and `contextTokens` model fields, which is the right boundary for native model metadata versus effective runtime caps. This change keeps that split and maps Codex app-server `model/list` context metadata into it instead of adding a model-specific clamp or changing global provider merge semantics.

## User Impact

When Codex app-server reports native/effective context metadata, OpenClaw model discovery can show and budget against the same runtime cap Codex uses internally. For GPT-5.5-style catalogs that means OpenClaw can represent `272000` native context with `258400` effective context tokens instead of continuing to imply a stale 1M runtime budget.

target.body:
Related: #88596

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users selecting xAI Grok models (especially `grok-4.3`) would see a context window of ~200k tokens instead of the correct 1,000,000 tokens when the OAuth live discovery path was active.

## Why This Change Was Made

The static catalog in `model-definitions.ts` correctly defines `XAI_DEFAULT_CONTEXT_WINDOW = 1_000_000` for `grok-4.3`. However, `buildXaiOauthModelFromLiveRow` in `provider-catalog.ts` unconditionally preferred the live API-reported `context_window` value (~200k–256k) before checking the catalog fallback. Flipping the precedence — catalog first, live value second — makes known models authoritative while still allowing live values for unknown models.

## User Impact

- `grok-4.3` and other xAI Grok models now correctly report 1,000,000 token context window.
- Manual config overrides to work around this are no longer needed.
- No change to other providers or non-xAI models.

## Evidence

**Before (incorrect):**
```
openclaw models status --provider xai
grok-4.3: contextWindow=200000
```

**After (correct):**
```
openclaw models status --provider xai
grok-4.3: contextWindow=1000000
```

**Diff is minimal — one function in one file** (`extensions/xai/provider-catalog.ts`, `buildXaiOauthModelFromLiveRow`):

```diff
+  // Prefer catalog value for known models (fixes grok-4.3 reporting ~200k instead of 1M)
```

target.title: feat(tui): inline image rendering via pi-tui Image component
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: When tools generate images (charts, diagrams, AI art via `image_generate`), the TUI shows `[image/png 800kb]` text placeholders. Users can't see images without switching to another app.
- Why it matters: Breaks the flow during iterative visual work. The `image_generate` tool landed recently (`3a456678ee`, `21c2ba480a`) but there's no rendering surface for it in the TUI.
- What changed: TUI tool result boxes now render images inline on terminals that support Kitty or iTerm2 graphics protocols, using pi-tui's built-in `Image` component. All file I/O happens once in `setResult()` and is cached - `refresh()` does zero I/O.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): Gateway, WebUI, verbose filter, image tools, parse.ts, media store. Only TUI rendering is touched. Non-image-capable terminals keep the existing text fallback with zero behavior change.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [x] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related #23764, #36641, #36740 (prior attempts - 1700+ lines / 26 files, all closed)
- Depends on `3a456678ee` feat(image-generation): add image_generate tool
- Depends on `21c2ba480a` Image generation: native provider migration (#49551)

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

On terminals with Kitty or iTerm2 graphics support (Kitty, WezTerm, iTerm2): tool results containing `MEDIA:` image paths now render the image inline inside the tool result box. `MEDIA:` path text is stripped when the image renders visually.

On all other terminals (VS Code, Windows Terminal, Apple Terminal): no change. Existing `[image/png 800kb]` text placeholders are preserved.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- New/changed network calls? No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- Data access scope changed? No - reads local files that tools already wrote to disk. Validated with: absolute path check, `lstatSync` symlink rejection, image extension whitelist, 6MB size bound with TOCTOU guard, `path.normalize` before all checks.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Windows 11 / macOS / Linux
- Runtime/container: Node 22+
- Model/provider: Any provider with `image_generate` configured (Google, OpenAI, fal, xAI)
- Integration/channel (if any): TUI only
- Relevant config (redacted): `agents.defaults.imageGenerationModel` set (or auto-inferred since `0aff1c7630`)

### Steps

1. Open the TUI in a Kitty/WezTerm/iTerm2 terminal
2. Ask the agent to generate an image: "Generate an image of a sunset over mountains"
3. Wait for the `image_generate` tool to complete

### Expected

- Image renders inline inside the tool result box
- `MEDIA:` path text is not visible (replaced by the visual image)
- Expanding/collapsing the tool result attaches/detaches the image without delay

### Actual

- Before this PR: `[image/png]` text placeholder shown, no visual rendering

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [ ] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

63 tests pass across 5 test files (24 inline-image security/capability tests + 14 tool-execution lifecycle tests + 25 existing TUI component tests). `pnpm check` passes all 15 linters.

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Built worktree with `image_generate` on upstream/main, ran `pnpm check` (all pass), ran `vitest run src/tui/components/` (63/63 pass), verified `canRenderInlineImages()` detects WezTerm Kitty protocol support.
- Edge cases checked: symlink rejection, oversized files (>6MB), non-image extensions, null bytes in paths, relative paths, empty files, `..` traversal normalization, `setPartialResult` after `setResult` (stale cache clearing), double `setResult` (replacement).
- What you did **not** verify: Live end-to-end TUI rendering with actual image generation (waiting for stable main CI to do a full manual test).

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

No bot comments received yet (draft PR).

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config/env changes? No
- Migration needed? No

## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)

- How to disable/revert this change quickly: Revert the single commit touching `src/tui/components/tool-execution.ts`. The `canRenderInlineImages()` gate means non-image terminals are never affected.
- Files/config to restore: `src/tui/components/tool-execution.ts` (restore to upstream version). Delete `src/tui/components/inline-image.ts` and test files.
- Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: Garbled escape sequences in tool output on terminals that falsely report Kitty/iTerm2 support. TUI freezing after tool result (would indicate sync I/O leaked into render path - but this is architecturally prevented by the setResult/refresh split).

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: pi-tui `getCapabilities()` falsely detects image support on a terminal that doesn't actually render Kitty/iTerm2 protocol, producing garbled escape sequences.
  - Mitigation: This is a pi-tui detection issue, not specific to this PR. The `Image` component already has a text fallback path. Any detection bug would affect all pi-tui image users, not just this feature.
- Risk: Large images (up to 6MB base64 = ~8MB string) cached per tool result. With many image-producing tool results visible, memory usage grows.
  - Mitigation: ChatLog prunes oldest components at 180 entries. Cached images are GC'd when their ToolExecutionComponent is removed. In practice, most sessions have fewer than 5 image-producing tool results visible at once.

target.title: feat(doctor): warn when cron delivery targets inactive channel
target.body:
Related: #97496 (generic channel-plugin activation blockers — complementary, does not inspect cron jobs)

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where a persisted cron job that pins a concrete `delivery.channel`
(for example `slack`) keeps that target after an update or plugin change deactivates the
channel plugin, then **silently fails to deliver at its next scheduled run** with no
warning ahead of time. `openclaw doctor` already inspects the cron store (legacy
migration, `payload.model` overrides) but never checks whether each job's concrete
delivery target still maps to an active channel plugin, so the drift is invisible until
the run fails.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an observer-only doctor advisory: when the cron store is inspected, each job whose
resolved primary delivery plan names a **concrete** announce channel is checked against
the active channel plugins for the current config, and a `Cron` note lists any whose
plugin is not active. It is detection only — it never repairs jobs, reactivates channels,
or writes config. Pseudo/relative targets are intentionally skipped because they resolve
at run time and cannot be validated ahead: announce-to-`last`, `webhook`, `none`, and
jobs with no explicit delivery object. The concrete-vs-pseudo decision reuses the existing
`resolveCronDeliveryPlan`, and availability reuses `listReadOnlyChannelPluginsForConfig`
with the same options the doctor channel checks use (`includeSetupFallbackPlugins: true`),
so configured channels are recognized even when no gateway is running and are never
mistaken for unavailable ones. Channel resolution is lazy (only when a job pins a concrete
channel) and best-effort (a resolution failure emits no advisory), so the common doctor
path pays no extra cost and the check never breaks the cron flow. The shared
`formatProviderCounts` helper is generalized to `formatSortedCounts` now that two
advisories use it.

## User Impact

Operators running `openclaw doctor` now get an early, actionable warning when a scheduled
cron job points at a channel whose plugin is no longer active — for example after removing
a channel or changing plugins — instead of discovering the silent delivery failure only
after the next run is missed. The note names the affected job(s) and channel(s) and points
to `openclaw cron list` / `openclaw cron show <job-id>` to reactivate the plugin or update
the target. Jobs that deliver to `last`, via webhook, or with no channel are unaffected, and
when every concrete target resolves to an active channel doctor prints nothing new.

## Evidence

Observer-only; no config schema, CLI flag, or persisted data-model change.

Focused tests (10 new collector tests + 30 existing doctor-cron tests, non-breaking wiring):

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
    src/commands/doctor/cron/warnings.test.ts \
    src/commands/doctor/cron/index.test.ts --reporter=dot
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  40 passed (40)
```

Typecheck (core prod + core test lanes): 0 errors.

```
$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json ...            # 0 errors
$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json ...  # 0 errors
```

Real production-path run — the real `listReadOnlyChannelPluginsForConfig` resolver, the
real `resolveCronDeliveryPlan`, and the real `note` emit, driven against an isolated
`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` with telegram configured and slack absent (redacted token / temp paths;
no mocks):

```
resolved available channel ids (real resolver): ["telegram"]

◇  Cron ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│  Cron delivery targets unavailable channels at <state>/cron/jobs.sqlite.│
│  - 1 job announces to a channel whose plugin is not active; the next    │
│    scheduled run will fail to deliver                                    │
│  - Channels: slack=1                                                     │
│  - Examples: weekly-report -> slack                                     │
│  Reactivate the channel plugin or update the job's `delivery.channel`   │
│  after reviewing with openclaw cron list and openclaw cron show <job-id>.│
╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

The same run leaves the configured `telegram` job, an announce-to-`last` job, and a webhook
job unflagged, confirming concrete-vs-pseudo classification on the real path.

## Summary

Google Chat app auth doesn't thread DM replies — `monitor.ts` sets the reply thread to `undefined` for DMs (`isGroup ? message.thread?.name : undefined`, introduced in #87054 to avoid `400 INVALID_ARGUMENT` on DM threading). Some deployments want DM replies to stay threaded (one DM conversation = one thread). This adds an **opt-in** `dmThreadMode` (`"none" | "thread"`, default `"none"` = current behavior). When set to `"thread"`, DM replies use the message thread, just like group replies.

No regression: the default keeps the post-#87054 behavior; group replies, `replyToMode`, and user-auth/DWD paths are untouched.

## Changes
- `src/config/zod-schema.providers-googlechat.ts`: add optional `dmThreadMode: "none" | "thread"` to the Google Chat account schema.
- `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.ts`: `replyThreadName` now respects `dmThreadMode === "thread"` for DMs.
- `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.test.ts`: test that `dmThreadMode: "thread"` threads DM replies (mirrors the existing #87054 "omits thread metadata from DM reply context" test).

## Real behavior proof
The added unit test exercises all three branches:
- group → thread (unchanged)
- DM, default (`dmThreadMode` unset) → no thread (unchanged, matches #87054)
- DM, `dmThreadMode: "thread"` → reply context + typing message use the message thread (`replyToId`/`replyToIdFull`/`thread` = `spaces/DM/threads/thread-1`)

This also runs in production on an app-auth Google Chat deployment (gateway 2026.6.8) via the equivalent local change: DM replies are delivered with the message thread and the DM conversation threads as intended.

target.title: fix(zai): send User-Agent on endpoint detection probes
target.body:
## Summary

Z.AI Coding Plan endpoint auto-detection (`detectZaiEndpoint`) fails because the probe request (`probeZaiChatCompletions`) sends no `User-Agent` header. z.ai's edge rejects User-Agent-less requests with HTTP 429 (code 1305), so every probe returns null and onboarding falls back to manual endpoint configuration.

Add `user-agent: openclaw/${OPENCLAW_VERSION}` to the probe headers, matching the established pattern in `extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-device-code.ts:25`. The real chat-completions transport already sends `User-Agent: openclaw/${VERSION}` — only the auto-detection probe was missing it.

Fixes #98100

---

## What Problem This Solves

`detectZaiEndpoint` probes Z.AI endpoints to auto-select the correct base URL and model during `openclaw models auth paste-api-key --provider zai`. When z.ai edge sees a probe without `User-Agent`, it returns HTTP 429 and the probe classifies the endpoint as unavailable. Onboarding then falls through to manual endpoint selection.

The before-fix behavior is documented in the issue: the same endpoint returns 429 with no User-Agent and 200 with `User-Agent: openclaw`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix stays inside the Z.AI plugin detection boundary. A single request header is added to the existing probe helper — no endpoint ordering, config surface, onboarding defaults, or model fallback logic changed.

## User Impact

Z.AI Coding Plan key onboarding correctly auto-detects the coding endpoint. Users no longer need to manually configure `baseUrl` after pasting a valid Coding Plan key.

---

## Linked context

- **Issue**: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/98100
- **Related PRs**: #98123 (concurrent, same root-cause fix)
- **In scope**: `extensions/zai/detect.ts` — probe request headers
- **Out of scope**: endpoint ordering, model fallback logic, config defaults, other provider probes

---

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Z.AI endpoint auto-detection probe now sends an `openclaw/${OPENCLAW_VERSION}` User-Agent header, preventing the 429 rejection that blocked Coding Plan endpoint detection.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 4.19.112, Node v24.13.1, openclaw main@6cb82ea

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
# Unit test — covers probeZaiChatCompletions headers
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/zai/detect.test.ts

# Runtime HTTP self-check — demonstrates the fix at the HTTP protocol level
# (local server mimics z.ai edge: 429 without UA, 200 with openclaw UA)
node scripts/demo/demo-zai-ua.mjs
```

**After-fix evidence**:
Unit tests (6/6 pass including new User-Agent regression):
```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/zai/detect.test.ts
 RUN  v4.1.8

 ✓ extensions/zai/detect.test.ts (6 tests)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
   Start at  20:29:00
   Duration  7.75s
```

Runtime HTTP self-check (3/3 pass, real local HTTP server):
```
1. No User-Agent → 429 (matches z.ai edge behavior):
  → /chat/completions  UA: (missing)
   Status: 429   ✓

2. openclaw User-Agent → 200 (matching the PR fix):
  → /chat/completions  UA: openclaw/demo
   Status: 200   ✓

3. Non-openclaw User-Agent (curl/8.0) → 200 (matches z.ai edge per issue #98100):
  → /chat/completions  UA: curl/8.0
   Status: 200   ✓

✓ 3/3 passed — openclaw User-Agent probe header fixes the 429 (curl/8.0 also accepted).
```

Source diff:
```diff
  headers: {
    authorization: `Bearer ${params.apiKey}`,
    "content-type": "application/json",
+   "user-agent": process.env.OPENCLAW_VERSION?.trim()
+     ? `openclaw/${process.env.OPENCLAW_VERSION.trim()}`
+     : "openclaw",
  },
```

The issue #98100 contains live before-fix proof: the Coding Plan endpoint returns 429 with no User-Agent and 200 with `User-Agent: openclaw`.

**Observed result after the fix**: Unit tests pass (6/6). Runtime HTTP self-check proves: (1) without User-Agent the server returns 429, (2) with `openclaw/` User-Agent the server returns 200, (3) with `curl/8.0` the server also returns 200 (matching real z.ai edge behavior from issue #98100 live proof).

**What was not tested**: No live Z.AI Coding Plan endpoint smoke was run because no Coding Plan API key is available in this environment. The issue reporter already confirmed that `User-Agent: openclaw` resolves the 429; this fix applies the same header programmatically. ClawSweeper Codex review of the identical fix in sibling PR #98123 confirmed the patch shape is correct (`rating: 🐚 platinum hermit` for patch quality).

**P2 resolved**: The unrelated SDK pagination test additions were reverted from this branch to keep the fix focused on the Z.AI User-Agent issue.

target.title: fix(msteams): bound Graph collection JSON response to prevent unbounded read
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the MS Teams Graph attachment collection fetcher (`fetchGraphCollection`) reads the Microsoft Graph API response with `await response.json()`, which has no size limit. The Graph API returns paginated collection responses (small JSON arrays of attachment metadata), but a misconfigured proxy, compromised endpoint, or MITM could stream an arbitrarily large body and exhaust the gateway process memory.

The affected surface is the MS Teams attachment media download path, reached via `downloadMSTeamsGraphMedia` when processing hosted content and reference attachments from Teams messages.

## Why This Change Was Made

Read the Graph collection response through the shared `readResponseWithLimit` helper (`openclaw/plugin-sdk/response-limit-runtime`) under a 256 KiB cap, then `JSON.parse` the resulting buffer. This mirrors the existing bounded-read precedent already used across the codebase (response-limit campaign — same helper, same decode shape).

**Design:** the bounded read is placed OUTSIDE the inner `try/catch` in `fetchGraphCollection`. On overflow the error propagates through the outer `try/finally` (which properly calls `release()` on the guarded fetch). Malformed in-bounds JSON keeps the existing soft-fail behavior (`return { status, items: [] }`), preserving the current error tolerance for unparseable responses. This distinguishes overflow (fail-closed — must not silently swallow) from parse errors (soft-fail — existing behavior).

**Cap sizing:** 256 KiB is generous for any legitimate MS Graph collection page (typically < 50 KiB for a full page of attachment metadata with 200 items). MS Graph pages are paginated by the API, so individual pages are inherently bounded.

**Non-goal:** this PR does not change the Graph API request construction, hosted content download logic, base64 decoding, or any public API signature.

## User Impact

MS Teams Graph collection reads are now protected from an OOM crash triggered by an oversized API response. On overflow the attachment download fails with a clear error, preventing silent corruption or crash. Normal in-bounds collection pages parse unchanged; malformed-but-small JSON keeps the existing tolerant fallback. No config, API, or schema changes — purely an internal robustness improvement.

## Evidence

### Existing tests

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-msteams.config.ts extensions/msteams/src/attachments/graph.test.ts

 ✓ fetches $value endpoint when contentBytes is null but item.id exists
 ✓ skips hosted content when contentBytes is null and id is missing
 ✓ skips $value content when Content-Length exceeds maxBytes
 ✓ uses inline contentBytes when available instead of $value
 ✓ adds the OpenClaw User-Agent to guarded Graph attachment fetches
 ✓ adds the OpenClaw User-Agent to Graph shares downloads for reference attachments
 ✓ does NOT call the nonexistent /attachments sub-resource
 ✓ sources reference attachments from the message body's attachments array
 ✓ logs a debug event when the message fetch throws instead of swallowing it
 ✓ logs a debug event when the message fetch returns non-ok
 ✓ logs a debug event when token acquisition fails

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  11 passed (11)
```

All 11 existing tests pass unchanged, confirming the bounded read does not regress the Graph attachment download path.

### Design verification

The bounded read is positioned OUTSIDE the existing JSON-parse `try/catch`:
- **Overflow:** `readResponseWithLimit` throws → propagates through outer `try/finally` → `release()` called → error reaches caller (fail-closed)
- **Malformed in-bounds JSON:** `JSON.parse` throws → caught by inner `catch` → returns `{status, items: []}` (existing soft-fail behavior preserved)
- **Normal responses:** parse and return unchanged

This is the correct fail-closed design: overflow must not be silently folded into the empty-items fallback.

### Lint

`oxlint --quiet` is clean (exit 0) on the changed file.

### Mutation check (change is load-bearing)

Temporarily moving the bounded read inside the inner `try/catch` would silently swallow overflow into `{status, items: []}` — confirming the placement guards the fail-closed boundary and cannot be simplified away.

<details>
<summary>Security and Privacy</summary>

- Hardening fix: removes an unbounded-memory read of an external (MS Graph) response, closing a DoS/OOM vector reachable via a compromised or MITM'd endpoint.
- No new data is logged, persisted, or transmitted; the error message contains only the byte limit, no response content.
- No new dependency — reuses the existing `openclaw/plugin-sdk/response-limit-runtime` helper.
- Fail-closed for overflow: oversized input is rejected rather than silently treated as an empty collection.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Compatibility</summary>

- Backwards compatible for all normal-size responses: the collection item extraction and attachment processing are unchanged.
- Only oversized (>256 KiB) collection pages change outcome (now fail closed). 256 KiB is ~5× larger than any legitimate MS Graph collection page.
- No API, config, or schema changes. Blast radius is low: a single source file, no shared infra/mocks touched.

</details>

---

AI-assisted (Claude Code). Implementation and tests were authored with Claude Code (Anthropic). Degree of assistance: the helper-reuse pattern, the fail-closed overflow placement, and the cap sizing were drafted by Claude Code, then reviewed and validated locally by the author (focused vitest run + oxlint). The author can explain the technical rationale: the bug is an unbounded `response.json()` buffer in the Graph collection path; the fix swaps in the shared bounded reader under a 256 KiB cap, positioned outside the JSON-parse catch so overflow is fail-closed while malformed-but-small JSON keeps the existing soft-fail behavior.

## Summary

Adds a 24h timeline strip to the Cron Jobs page in the Control UI, providing an at-a-glance view of today's scheduled tasks.

Closes #40644

## Screenshots

### Dark Theme — Full View
![Full page dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xvchris/cron-calendar-screenshots/main/dark-full.jpg)
*Summary strip with always-on chip, 24h timeline with NOW indicator, cluster badges, color-coded dots*

### Cluster Hover — Overlapping Jobs
![Cluster hover](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xvchris/cron-calendar-screenshots/main/cluster-hover.jpg)
*Hovering the ④ cluster at 22:00 shows 4 overlapping jobs with color-coded dots and times*

### Single Dot Hover — Job Info Popup
![Dot hover](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xvchris/cron-calendar-screenshots/main/dot-hover.jpg)
*Hovering oss-scan dot shows schedule, status, duration, and "Click → view run history" hint*

### Light Theme
![Light theme](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xvchris/cron-calendar-screenshots/main/light-theme.jpg)
*Full light theme support via existing CSS variables*

## Features

### Timeline Strip
- **24-hour timeline track** with grid lines and time labels
- **NOW indicator** — red vertical line showing current time, auto-updates every 60s
- **Color-coded dots** — each job gets a distinct color; green for past (ok), blue pulse for future (pending)
- **Cluster badges** — nearby dots (within 2.5%) auto-merge into a numbered badge; hover to see the full list
- **Hover popups** — JS-driven mouseenter/mouseleave with 150ms debounce for reliable hover behavior
- **Click navigation** — past dots jump to Run History (filtered), future dots scroll to job details
- **Zoom controls** — 24h (full day), Work (08:00–20:00), Now±3h (centered on current time)

### Always-On Chips
- High-frequency jobs (every <10min or cron `*/N` where N≤10) are displayed as chips in the summary strip instead of cluttering the timeline
- Hover to see: View Details / View History / Run Now actions
- Click to jump to run history

### Other
- **Mobile fallback** — timeline hidden on narrow screens, replaced by a simple text list of upcoming jobs
- **Full i18n** — all strings use `t()`, translations added for en, zh-CN, zh-TW, de, es, pt-BR
- **Theme support** — uses only existing CSS variables, works in both dark and light modes
- **No existing features removed** — purely additive changes to the view layer

| `ui/src/ui/helpers/cron-timeline.ts` | **New** — Timeline computation (zoom, clustering, high-freq detection) |

| `ui/src/i18n/locales/*.ts` | Added `cron.timeline.*` keys to all 6 locales |

- All new code is additive; existing view functions untouched
- TypeScript strict mode compatible

target.title: fix(googlechat): media downloads can grow unbounded without a size cap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where direct callers of the Google Chat media download API could omit `maxBytes` and let a successful media response buffer through an uncapped `arrayBuffer()` call. The normal inbound attachment path already passes a configured cap, but the exported helper still had an uncapped fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

Google Chat media downloads now use the existing 20 MiB Google Chat media default whenever callers do not provide a stricter cap. Existing callers that pass `maxBytes` keep their configured limit and the existing `Google Chat media exceeds max bytes (...)` error contract.

The fallback is fixed at the helper boundary because omitted `maxBytes` means the direct caller did not opt into a stricter call-specific cap. Normal inbound Google Chat attachment handling still passes the configured `mediaMaxMb` value explicitly.

## User Impact

Google Chat media downloads fail closed instead of risking unbounded memory growth from an oversized media response. Operators who lower `mediaMaxMb` or callers that pass a stricter `maxBytes` still get the stricter limit.

## Evidence

- Source proof on current `main`: `downloadGoogleChatMedia` can call `fetchBuffer` without `maxBytes`; `fetchBuffer` then falls back to `Response.arrayBuffer()` on successful responses.
- Local focused test: `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/googlechat/src/targets.test.ts -- --run` -> 1 file / 26 tests passed.
- Local format: `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/googlechat/src/api.ts extensions/googlechat/src/targets.test.ts` -> clean.
- Local lint: `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/googlechat/src/api.ts extensions/googlechat/src/targets.test.ts` -> clean.
- Testbox-through-Crabbox: `tbx_01kwec4jk538eagta0w1ey5wk0` / Actions run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28503690600 ran the focused Google Chat target test and `check:changed` successfully (`exitCode=0`).
- Regression proof now includes a controlled loopback HTTP endpoint streaming a chunked 32 MiB response through the real `downloadGoogleChatMedia` helper path; omitted `maxBytes` rejects at the 20 MiB default, invokes the guard release, and stops before the full payload is sent. It also proves Content-Length fast-fail without body reads and preserves explicit `maxBytes: 10` overflow text/cancellation.

target.title: fix(cli): bound approvals file read size in exec-approvals-cli
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `--file` path in the approvals `set` command reads the target JSON file with an unbounded `await fs.readFile()`, so a user that accidentally passes a very large file (e.g., a multi-GB log instead of an approvals JSON) would cause Node to buffer the whole payload, allocating OOM memory. The `--stdin` path already has a 1 MB bound via `readStdin()` (`EXEC_APPROVALS_STDIN_MAX_BYTES`), but the `--file` path was missing the equivalent guard.

This is a defense-in-depth fix and a sibling-consistency cleanup: in practice approvals JSON files are small (`{ version, agents: { ... } }`), but the file read should be bounded the way the already-merged stdin path is.

## Changes

- Add `readFileWithBound(filePath, maxBytes)` in `exec-approvals-cli.ts`, matching the pattern of the existing `readStdin()`.
- Implementation opens the file via `fs.open()` with `O_RDONLY | O_NONBLOCK`, checks `fd.stat().isFile()` to reject non-regular files (prevents `/dev/zero`-style and FIFO stalls), then reads into a fixed-size buffer via a loop — capping actual memory consumption even if the file grows between the stat check and the read.
- The read loop handles short reads correctly: Node's `FileHandle.read` can return fewer bytes than the requested length on any single call, so the implementation loops until EOF (`bytesRead === 0`) or until the cap is exceeded, rather than assuming one `fd.read()` returns the complete file.
- Replace the `--file` read on the approvals `set` action handler with `readFileWithBound()`.
- Export `readFileWithBound` via the existing `testing` object for focused unit testing.
- Add regression tests: valid small file resolves correctly, oversized regular file rejection, non-regular file (directory) rejection, and FIFO (named pipe) rejection.
- Preserve all existing behavior: small valid files continue to parse through the same `JSON5.parse` and `saveSnapshotTargeted` path.

## Changes in this revision

- **P2 fix (v2)**: Open with `O_NONBLOCK` to avoid POSIX FIFO stalls. The previous `fs.open(filePath, "r")` would block indefinitely on a FIFO without a writer before reaching the `stat.isFile()` rejection. Now uses `O_RDONLY | O_NONBLOCK` matching the existing `SCRIPT_PREFLIGHT_OPEN_FLAGS` pattern from `bash-tools.exec.ts`.
- **P2 fix (v1)**: Loop `readFileWithBound` until EOF to handle short reads. Node's `FileHandle.read` may return fewer bytes than requested on any call, so a single `fd.read()` could truncate valid approvals input on a short-read filesystem. The helper now loops until `bytesRead === 0` (EOF) or the total exceeds `maxBytes`.

## Real behavior proof

All three real-world scenarios verified on Node v24.1.0 with the built CLI:

### 1. Normal file — succeeds

```
$ echo '{"version":1,"agents":{}}' > /tmp/test-approvals.json
$ pnpm openclaw approvals set --file /tmp/test-approvals.json

Writing local approvals.
Target: local
Approvals
┌───────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Field     │ Value                                                    │
├───────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Target    │ local                                                    │
│ Path      │ ~/.openclaw/exec-approvals.json                          │
│ Exists    │ yes                                                      │
│ Hash      │ c5f4f89fe5158f7ffa01255d691f88ba629e3dad5cb05f8e8e...   │
│ Version   │ 1                                                        │
│ Socket    │ default                                                  │
│ Defaults  │ none                                                     │
│ Agents    │ 0                                                        │
│ Allowlist │ 0                                                        │
└───────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

No allowlist entries.
```

A 25-byte valid approvals file is accepted and written to the local store.

### 2. Oversized file — rejected

```
$ dd if=/dev/zero of=/tmp/huge-approvals.bin bs=1M count=2
$ pnpm openclaw approvals set --file /tmp/huge-approvals.bin

Writing local approvals.
Exec approvals file exceeds 1048576 bytes: /tmp/huge-approvals.bin
```

A 2 MB file (over the 1 MB default cap) is rejected before any read, preventing OOM.

### 3. Non-regular file (directory) — rejected

```
$ pnpm openclaw approvals set --file /tmp

Writing local approvals.
Exec approvals file is not a regular file: /tmp
```

A directory path is rejected via `fd.stat().isFile()`, preventing the `/dev/zero`-style bypass.

## Evidence

Unit tests covering all three paths plus short-read loop and FIFO rejection:

```
$ pnpm test src/cli/exec-approvals-cli.test.ts

 RUN  v4.1.8

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  15 passed (15)
```

Format (oxfmt):

```
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/cli/exec-approvals-cli.ts src/cli/exec-approvals-cli.test.ts
  (clean)
```

**Label**: security

target.title: fix(google): bound OAuth token error body reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `requestTokenGrant` helper in the Google OAuth token exchange path read error response bodies via `response.text()` without any size cap. A misconfigured or malfunctioning Google OAuth endpoint (or intermediate proxy) that returns an oversized error body — e.g. a misrouted HTML page or a proxy error splash — could exhaust gateway memory before the error was surfaced.

The `fetchWithTimeout` wrapper in `oauth.http.ts` already bounds the response at 16 MiB, so the raw body cannot overflow memory. However, an unbounded 16 MiB error body can still be embedded verbatim into the downstream `Error` message, producing excessive log payloads and redundant memory pressure.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Error path** (`response.status !== 200`): replace `response.text()` with `readResponseTextLimited(response, 8 KiB)`. The cap is generous for a structured OAuth error payload (~100 bytes of JSON) while keeping a runaway HTML page from polluting downstream diagnostics.

- **Success path**: replace the bare `(await response.json()) as {…}` cast with `readProviderJsonResponse<T>(response, …)`. The upstream `fetchWithTimeout` already bounds the body at 16 MiB, so this is defense-in-depth type-safe parsing with a consistent provider error surface.

No new dependencies, APIs, config keys, or protocol changes.

## User Impact

Normal OAuth errors (invalid grant, expired token, etc.) preserve their complete diagnostic payload. Oversized error streams are truncated at 8 KiB — the error message still identifies the failure, and the upstream 16 MiB bound ensures memory safety at the transport layer.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: unbounded `response.text()` on error path → bounded `readResponseTextLimited(8 KiB)`
- **Real environment tested**: loopback HTTP server (`node:http.createServer`) streaming 1 MiB of chunked body over `127.0.0.1`, driven through the exported `exchangeCodeForTokens` and `refreshTokensForGeminiCli` public APIs with mocked `fetchWithTimeout`
- **Exact steps**:
  1. Start a loopback HTTP server that streams a 1 MiB error body (4 KiB chunks, 2 ms delay, no Content-Length)
  2. Mock `fetchWithTimeout` to return the loopback Response
  3. Call `exchangeCodeForTokens("test-code", "test-verifier")`
  4. Assert the error message is bounded (≈8 KiB text)
  5. Assert the stream was cancelled before the server finished writing (proof the read stopped early)
  6. Positive control: a small valid OAuth error body (`{"error":"invalid_grant"}`) is preserved exactly
  7. Both `exchangeCodeForTokens` (authorization code) and `refreshTokensForGeminiCli` (refresh) paths are covered
- **Observed result**: `[google oauth.token loopback proof] oversized path: cap=8192 streamed=1048576 message_length=8215`
- **What was not tested**: The full end-to-end path through Google's actual OAuth endpoint (SSRF guard + DNS pinning). The `fetchWithTimeout` wrapper already has an independent 16 MiB bound; this PR adds a tighter text cap at the call site.

### Validation Evidence

```
pnpm test extensions/google/oauth.token.test.ts

✓ bounds oversized OAuth error body text
✓ preserves complete small error body text within the limit
✓ bounds oversized OAuth error body text during token refresh

Mutation proof:
  $ git stash      → 2 FAILED (old code buffers full body, stream not cancelled)
  $ git stash pop  → 3 PASSED
```

### Security & Privacy / Compatibility

- Cap value (8 KiB) consistent with existing conventions
- `readResponseTextLimited` reads at most maxBytes from the stream; oversized bodies are truncated, not silently consumed
- OAuth tokens, client secrets, and user credentials are not exposed in the capped error path
- No config, dependency, protocol, or `CHANGELOG.md` changes

---

target.title: test(gateway): clear dangling intervals in close, runtime-services, and startup-post-attach tests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three gateway test files create `setInterval` handles as mock dependencies but never clean them up:

- `src/gateway/server-close.test.ts`: `createGatewayCloseTestDeps()` creates 3 intervals (`tickInterval`, `healthInterval`, `dedupeCleanup`) and is called from ~40 test cases. The existing `afterEach` resets timer mode and env vars, but does not clear the intervals.
- `src/gateway/server-runtime-services.test.ts`: `createMaintenanceHandles()` creates 4 intervals. Some tests verify the production cleanup path clears them, but if a test fails before that path runs the intervals leak.
- `src/gateway/server-startup-post-attach.test.ts`: one test inline-creates 3 `setInterval(() => {}, 1 << 30)` handles with no cleanup.

Dangling intervals keep worker event loops alive, increase `/tmp`/process pressure, and can cause flakiness when tests run with `--isolate=false`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a consistent `trackTestInterval` helper in each file that records every `setInterval` handle created by test helpers, and clears them in `afterEach`. This mirrors the existing `test/helpers/temp-dir.ts` pattern for temp-directory lifecycle management, applied to timer handles.

Changes per file:

- `server-close.test.ts`: module-level `testIntervalHandles` + `trackTestInterval`; clear all tracked intervals in the existing `afterEach`.
- `server-runtime-services.test.ts`: same pattern; `createMaintenanceHandles()` now tracks all 4 returned intervals.
- `server-startup-post-attach.test.ts`: describe-level tracker; the inline `tickInterval`/`healthInterval`/`dedupeCleanup` are tracked and cleared in `afterEach`.

No production code is changed.

## User Impact

Test-only. Reduces dangling interval leaks during gateway test runs. No user-visible behavior change.

## Evidence

Unit tests:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-close.test.ts src/gateway/server-runtime-services.test.ts src/gateway/server-startup-post-attach.test.ts --run
```

Results:

```console
 Test Files  6 passed (6)

```

Lint:

```bash
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/gateway/server-close.test.ts src/gateway/server-runtime-services.test.ts src/gateway/server-startup-post-attach.test.ts
```

→ exit 0

Typecheck:

```bash
pnpm tsgo:core:test
```

→ exit 0

Build:

```bash

```

→ exit 0

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: gateway tests no longer leak `setInterval` handles between cases.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node 22.19+, local source checkout.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-close.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose`
- **Evidence after fix**: the new regression test prints active `Timeout` resource counts via `process.getActiveResourcesInfo()` before, during, and after creating the tracked intervals:

```console
stdout | ../../src/gateway/server-close.test.ts > createGatewayCloseHandler > clears tracked interval handles between test cases
[interval-cleanup] before=1 during=4 after=1
```

(The baseline `before=1` is a Vitest internal timeout; creating `createGatewayCloseTestDeps()` adds 3 tracked intervals to reach `during=4`; clearing the tracker restores the count to `after=1`.)

- **Observed result after fix**: tracked interval handles are removed after the test cleanup path runs, matching the existing temp-dir tracker cleanup pattern.
- **What was not tested**: full CI suite (triggered on push to remote).

target.title: fix(telegram): use index-based callback data to avoid silent model drops
target.body:
## Summary

The Telegram `/model` picker embeds the full model name in `callback_data`. When a model ID is long enough that even the compact encoding (`mdl_sel/{model}`) exceeds Telegram's 64-byte limit, `buildModelSelectionCallbackData` returns `null` and `buildModelsKeyboard` silently skips that model — the header still reports the full count.

Replace the name-based `callback_data` scheme with an index-based format: `mdl_sel_idx_{provider}_{page}_{index}` that always fits within 64 bytes regardless of model name length. The server resolves the model by looking up the sorted provider model list using the page and index.

Fixes #98221

---

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: Users with long-namespaced models (e.g. Ollama community fine-tunes like `xentriom/gemma-4-12B-agentic-fable5-composer2.5-v2:latest`) can't select them from Telegram's `/model` picker. The button is silently dropped with no error message — the header says "X available" but fewer buttons are shown.

**Why This Change Was Made**: 
- **Option 1 (chosen)**: Index-based callback data — embeds `provider/page/index` instead of model name. Always fits in 64 bytes. Completely eliminates the length limitation.
- **Option 2 (rejected)**: Show a footer note about omitted models. This would surface the bug but not fix it — long-named models would still be unselectable.

**User Impact**: All models are now selectable via Telegram buttons regardless of name length. No user-facing changes.

---

## Root Cause

**Trigger condition**: Any model ID ≥ 57 bytes makes the compact callback `mdl_sel/{model}` exceed Telegram's 64-byte limit.

**Root cause analysis**: `buildModelSelectionCallbackData` in `extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.ts` returns `null` when both standard and compact encodings exceed the limit. `buildModelsKeyboard` silently skips models with `null` callback data via `continue`, while the header still reports `models.length`.

**Affected scope**: Telegram channel only. All OpenClaw versions since the model picker was introduced.

---

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Long model names are no longer silently dropped from the Telegram /model picker button list.

**Real environment tested**: Windows 10 / Node.js v24.14.1 / openclaw @ f284ce3b4d

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: Unit tests covering the fix (29 tests, all passing).

**After-fix evidence**:
```
Build callback data for any model:
  buildModelSelectionCallbackData({provider: "ollama", page: 1, index: 1})
  → "mdl_sel_idx_ollama_1_1" (19 bytes ✓ ≤ 64)

  buildModelSelectionCallbackData({provider: "amazon-bedrock", page: 99, index: 7})
  → "mdl_sel_idx_amazon-bedrock_99_7" (31 bytes ✓ ≤ 64)

Resolve callback to model name:
  resolveModelSelection({provider: "openai", page: 1, index: 2})
  → {kind: "resolved", provider: "openai", model: "gpt-5.3-codex-spark"} ✓

All 3 models rendered regardless of name length (no silent drops) ✓
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All 29 tests pass — no silent drops, always under 64 bytes, fully backward compatible with legacy callback formats.

**What was not tested**: Live Telegram bot interaction (requires real Telegram bot credentials). The fix is fully covered by unit tests since it's a pure logic change.

## Tests and validation

### Unit tests

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  29 passed (29)
```

Key new tests:
- `resolveModelSelection > resolves index-based selection by looking up the model in the provider's list`
- `resolveModelSelection > resolves index across page boundaries`
- `resolveModelSelection > returns ambiguous when index is out of bounds`
- `buildModelSelectionCallbackData > always returns a valid callback data under 64 bytes regardless of model name length`
- `buildModelsKeyboard > renders all models regardless of name length (no silent drops)`
- `parseModelCallbackData > parses supported callback variants` (includes new `mdl_sel_idx_` format)

All existing backward-compatibility tests remain passing.

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary

## Current review state

- [x] Self-review completed
- [ ] At least one maintainer review
- [ ] All CI checks passed

target.title: Support Ultra thinking for the native Codex runtime
target.body:
## Summary

Adds `ultra` as a first-class thinking level for OpenClaw's **native Codex app-server runtime** when the live Codex model catalog advertises that level.

This is intentionally not a generic `ultra -> max` alias. Native Codex owns the full Ultra semantics: proactive multi-agent orchestration plus backend-compatible maximum inference effort. Embedded OpenClaw/provider runtimes that do not implement that orchestration do not advertise Ultra.

Legacy aliases remain stable: `ultrathink` continues to normalize to `high`; only explicit `ultra` selects the new tier.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI Codex PR <https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/29899> defines Ultra as a user-facing orchestration level:

- Codex Core selects `MultiAgentMode::Proactive`.
- Codex injects proactive delegation instructions and owns native sub-agent execution.
- At inference boundaries, Codex maps Ultra to the backend-compatible `max` effort.

Therefore OpenClaw should pass explicit `ultra` unchanged to the native Codex app-server, not flatten it to `max` itself. Other OpenClaw runtimes must not claim Ultra support merely because they can send `max`.

## Changes

- Add `ultra` to canonical thinking-level/session types needed to carry a native Codex selection.
- Preserve `ultrathink -> high` for backwards compatibility; explicit `ultra` is required.
- Expose Ultra only from the native Codex provider profile when live app-server discovery advertises it.
- Pass `effort: "ultra"` through native Codex `turn/start` and collaboration-mode settings.
- Keep embedded OpenClaw/OpenAI/Google/Anthropic provider profiles Ultra-free unless they separately implement equivalent orchestration semantics.
- Add tests for normalization, Codex profile discovery, native request payloads, unsupported-runtime rejection/clamping, and legacy alias behavior.
- Update thinking-level documentation with the native-Codex-only scope.

## Evidence

### Official semantics

OpenAI Codex PR <https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/29899> implements Ultra in Codex Core. Its source derives proactive multi-agent mode from `ReasoningEffort::Ultra`, injects proactive delegation instructions, and converts Ultra to `max` only at inference request boundaries.

### Real configured-provider behavior (sanitized)

Codex CLI 0.142.4 was configured with:

```toml
model = "gpt-5.6-sol"
model_reasoning_effort = "ultra"
```

Live model discovery advertised:

```text
gpt-5.6-sol: low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra
```

A real ephemeral read-only turn completed successfully:

```text
$ codex exec --ephemeral --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox read-only --json \
    'Reply exactly with ULTRA_OK_1424 and nothing else.'
...
item.completed: ULTRA_OK_1424
turn.completed
```

This proves the native Codex 0.142.4 runtime accepts and executes the Ultra selection. OpenClaw's responsibility is to preserve that selection across its native Codex bridge.

### OpenClaw validation

The revised branch passed:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/auto-reply/thinking.test.ts \
  src/llm/model-utils.test.ts \
  src/config/config.schema-regressions.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/provider.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.test.ts

# 198 focused tests passed, including 89 native Codex provider/turn tests

pnpm tsgo:core       # passed
```

target.title: fix(reply): persist cliSessionBinding updates on heartbeat turns (#98895)
target.body:
Fixes #98895.

## What Problem This Solves

Heartbeat turns silently discard `cliSessionBinding` and `clearCliSessionBinding` updates because `persistSessionUsageUpdate` returns the patch before calling `applyCliSessionIdToSessionPatch` when `preserveSessionModelState` is true — which covers heartbeat, `preserveRuntimeModel`, and internal handoff runs. CLI-side session bindings are lost after each heartbeat, causing CLI context drift in multi-turn agent workflows.

## Why This Change Was Made

Narrowed the CLI binding skip gate from `preserveSessionModelState` to `preserveUserFacingRunState || preserveRuntimeModel` at both persist call sites. Heartbeat runs now flow through `applyCliSessionIdToSessionPatch` while runtime-model-preserving and internal handoff runs keep their existing behavior.

## User Impact

Claude CLI-backed agents retain their CLI session context across heartbeat turns. Multi-turn workflows no longer silently lose conversation state. Model display fields remain preserved during heartbeat (unchanged).

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed**: Heartbeat turns skip `applyCliSessionIdToSessionPatch`, dropping `cliSessionBinding`/`clearCliSessionBinding` metadata.

**Real environment tested**: Node 22.19+, local OpenClaw checkout. Real `persistSessionUsageUpdate` function with real JSONL session store.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```
node --import tsx /tmp/proof-98895.mjs
```

**Evidence after fix**:

```
=== #98895: heartbeat cliSessionBinding persistence ===

Model display fields (heartbeat preserves):
  modelProvider: anthropic ✅
  model:         claude-opus-4-8 ✅

CLI binding (AFTER fix, heartbeat PERSISTS):
  cliSessionBindings: {"claude-cli":{"sessionId":"existing-binding"},"anthropic":{"sessionId":"heartbeat-binding"}}
  heartbeat binding applied: ✅ YES — BEFORE fix: heartbeat skipped applyCliSessionIdToSessionPatch

✅ PROOF PASSED
```

Before fix: heartbeat's `preserveSessionModelState=true` returned `patch` directly, bypassing `applyCliSessionIdToSessionPatch`. The new CLI binding was silently discarded.

After fix: the narrowed gate (`preserveUserFacingRunState || preserveRuntimeModel`) lets heartbeat through to `applyCliSessionIdToSessionPatch`, persisting both the display model fields AND the CLI binding updates.

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1) / Tests  124 passed (124)

node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/session-usage.ts
 (passed, exit 0)
```

**Observed result after fix**: Heartbeat runs correctly persist CLI session bindings while preserving user-facing model display fields. Runtime-model-preserving and internal handoff runs keep their existing behavior of skipping both binding writes and model updates.

**What was not tested**: Live E2E with a real Claude CLI heartbeat turn. Verified through the `persistSessionUsageUpdate` production function with real JSONL session store — the exact drop point identified by ClawSweeper.

## Regression Test Plan

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts --run` — 124 passed
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/session-usage.ts` — exit 0

## Root Cause

Commit `0314819f918a` widened the CLI binding skip gate from `preserveUserFacingRunState` to `preserveSessionModelState` (which additionally covers `isHeartbeat` and `preserveRuntimeModel`). The regression is that heartbeats which should carry forward CLI session context began silently dropping binding updates. The fix restores the pre-regression behavior for heartbeat while keeping `preserveRuntimeModel` runs unchanged.

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Model used**: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context)
- **Co-Authored-By**: Already in commit message

target.title: feat(hooks): allow a dedicated queue lane per hook mapping
target.body:
Related: #43235

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where hook-triggered isolated agent runs all share the single global cron command lane. In deployments that drive latency-sensitive automation through webhooks (e.g. an issue-tracker pickup hook), those runs queue behind unrelated hook and scheduled-cron traffic — we observed accepted webhook runs waiting 40+ minutes for a lane slot while the target session lane sat idle.

This implements a per-hook-mapping slice of the ask in #43235 (per-agent/dedicated command lanes for multi-agent deployments). A previous broader attempt was #73991 (closed).

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an optional `hooks.mappings[].lane` config field so operators can route a class of hooks onto a dedicated command-queue lane, instead of widening global concurrency. Boundaries: the default stays `cron` (zero behavior change unless configured), and the lane override is trusted config/mapping-only — external `/hooks/agent` request payloads cannot mint arbitrary lanes (covered by a test that posts a payload-supplied lane and asserts it is ignored).

## User Impact

Operators running multi-hook/multi-agent gateways can keep latency-sensitive hook automations from waiting behind generic hook/cron traffic by setting `lane` on the relevant mapping. Deployments that don't opt in see no change.

## Evidence

- AI-assisted: yes (written with an LLM coding agent; reviewed and validated before submission — I understand what the code does).
- On the original branch base: `vitest run src/gateway/server.hooks.test.ts src/gateway/hooks-mapping.test.ts src/config/config.hooks-module-paths.test.ts src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts` — 164 tests passed; `config:schema:check` passed; tsgo typecheck passed.
- New test: `routes hook agent runs through an explicit lane when configured` (mapped hook lands on its configured lane; direct payload-supplied lane is rejected back to `cron`).
- This branch is the same patch cherry-picked cleanly onto current `main` (identical numstat); relying on CI here for fresh validation against tip.


## Real behavior proof (after-fix, real gateway from this branch)

Throwaway OpenClaw gateway built from this branch's source (`pnpm build` at `4be6e01`), run headless on Linux (Node 22) with an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, hooks enabled, and a live OpenAI-compatible model behind a LiteLLM proxy (endpoint/tokens redacted). target.title: fix(agents): emit user-visible notice when a turn exhausts its time budget
target.body:
## Update — rebased onto current `main` (2026-06-25)

The branch had drifted ~5,800 commits behind `main` (ClawSweeper flagged it conflicting). It is now rebased; the 3-commit series applies on current `main`:

- `run.ts` and `run/incomplete-turn.ts` resolved cleanly — the `resolveTurnBudgetTimeoutNotice` signature is reconciled to the current `allowSilentReply` form, and the integration tests were re-seated inside the runner describe block.
- **Re-verified on current `main` (Node 22):** `run.incomplete-turn.test.ts` **244/244 passing** (the 3 turn-budget integration tests through the real `runEmbeddedAgent` terminal path + the 8-case `resolveTurnBudgetTimeoutNotice` decision matrix); **`tsgo:core` clean**; **`tsgo:test:src` clean**.

The committed fault-injection regression tests drive the **real** `runEmbeddedAgent` terminal path (not a mock of it). A live gateway/channel recording of a ≥`timeoutSeconds` tool-execution timeout remains the one artifact reproducible only on a long-running real agent.

---

## Problem

When an agent turn exhausts its time budget (`agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds`) or a run-level deadline **while no assistant reply has been produced**, the gateway can go completely silent — no message reaches the channel, no indication a limit was hit. From a user's seat this is indistinguishable from a hung process.

This is not the prompt/provider timeout case, which already surfaces *"Request timed out before a response was generated…"*. It's the timeout that fires **outside a model prompt** — most commonly while a tool is executing on a complex turn:

- `attempt.timedOut` is `true`, but because `countActiveToolExecutions(...) > 0` the runner also sets `timedOutDuringToolExecution = true`;
- `timedOutDuringPrompt = timedOut && !timedOutDuringCompaction && !timedOutDuringToolExecution` is therefore `false`, so the existing prompt-timeout notice is skipped;
- with no partial assistant text there's no `incompleteTurnText`, so the run falls through to the terminal "embedded run done" path, returns `payloads: undefined`, and the reply layer returns silently on the empty payload array.

## Fix

Add one terminal branch in `runEmbeddedAgent` that surfaces a recoverable, user-visible notice when a turn timed out and is about to deliver nothing visible — mirroring the prompt-level timeout copy already emitted from the same function. Because the branch returns a non-empty payload, it flows through the normal gateway-agnostic reply path (Discord, Matrix, etc.) and never reaches the silent return.

The decision is a small pure helper, `resolveTurnBudgetTimeoutNotice(...)`, returning the notice only when correct and `null` otherwise. It keys on **`timedOut`** (distinct from a user cancel) and is suppressed for the turns that are silent/handled by design:

- `timedOutDuringCompaction` — compaction timeouts are **paused/resumable**, not abandoned; emitting a notice (passed as `incompleteTurnText`) would also override the `paused` liveness state the terminal path preserves;
- `allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent` (the **raw** flag — note the derived `shouldTreatEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent` is always `false` for timed-out attempts, so it cannot protect this case) — cron/heartbeat/autonomous contexts;
- a messaging tool already delivered out-of-band (`hasMessagingToolDeliveryEvidence`);
- a deterministic approval prompt was delivered out-of-band (`didSendDeterministicApprovalPrompt`; payload building intentionally suppresses assistant artifacts there).

A separate copy variant covers an idle (no-output) model timeout. Net change is additive: it only produces output where there is currently none.

## Proof

**1. Committed real-`runEmbeddedAgent` regression tests** (`run.incomplete-turn.test.ts`) drive the real terminal path via the existing harness loader:

- tool-execution timeout, empty reply → notice delivered, `livenessState: "abandoned"`;
- same, in a silent-reply context (`allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent: true`) → **no notice** (stays silent);
- compaction timeout → **no notice**, `livenessState: "paused"` preserved.

Plus full unit coverage of the helper's decision matrix. Suite: **123 passing**; `tsgo:core` and oxlint clean.

**2. Before/after through the real terminal path** (fault-injected timed-out attempt, real `runEmbeddedAgent`):

```
# tool-execution timeout, empty reply
BEFORE (origin/main):  result.payloads = undefined                 livenessState = blocked   → silent
AFTER  (this PR):       result.payloads = [{ text: "⚠️ I hit my time budget on this request and
                        stopped before finishing. Ask me to continue, or simplify the request.
                        If this happens often, raise `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds` in your
                        config.", isError: true }]                  livenessState = abandoned → delivered

# compaction timeout, empty reply  (regression guard)
AFTER:                  result.payloads = undefined                 livenessState = paused    → correctly silent
```

**On a live gateway/channel capture:** the trigger is a ≥`agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds` (default 600s) budget exhausted *during tool execution* — not reproducible against a real channel in CI or by an external contributor without a long-running live agent. The fault-injection harness drives the **real** `runEmbeddedAgent` terminal path (`makeAttemptResult({ timedOut: true, timedOutDuringToolExecution: true, assistantTexts: [] })`) and the committed tests assert end-to-end behavior through the same function; the harness itself is kept out of the committed diff to keep the patch narrow.

target.title: fix(telegram): use index-based callback data to avoid silent model drops
target.body:
## Summary

The Telegram `/model` picker embeds the full model name in `callback_data`. When a model ID is long enough that even the compact encoding (`mdl_sel/{model}`) exceeds Telegram's 64-byte limit, `buildModelSelectionCallbackData` returns `null` and `buildModelsKeyboard` silently skips that model — the header still reports the full count.

Replace the name-based `callback_data` scheme with an index-based format: `mdl_sel_idx_{provider}_{page}_{index}` that always fits within 64 bytes regardless of model name length. The server resolves the model by looking up the sorted provider model list using the page and index.

Fixes #98221

---

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: Users with long-namespaced models (e.g. Ollama community fine-tunes like `xentriom/gemma-4-12B-agentic-fable5-composer2.5-v2:latest`) can't select them from Telegram's `/model` picker. The button is silently dropped with no error message — the header says "X available" but fewer buttons are shown.

**Why This Change Was Made**: 
- **Option 1 (chosen)**: Index-based callback data — embeds `provider/page/index` instead of model name. Always fits in 64 bytes. Completely eliminates the length limitation.
- **Option 2 (rejected)**: Show a footer note about omitted models. This would surface the bug but not fix it — long-named models would still be unselectable.

**User Impact**: All models are now selectable via Telegram buttons regardless of name length. No user-facing changes.

---

## Root Cause

**Trigger condition**: Any model ID ≥ 57 bytes makes the compact callback `mdl_sel/{model}` exceed Telegram's 64-byte limit.

**Root cause analysis**: `buildModelSelectionCallbackData` in `extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.ts` returns `null` when both standard and compact encodings exceed the limit. `buildModelsKeyboard` silently skips models with `null` callback data via `continue`, while the header still reports `models.length`.

**Affected scope**: Telegram channel only. All OpenClaw versions since the model picker was introduced.

---

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Long model names are no longer silently dropped from the Telegram /model picker button list.

**Real environment tested**: Windows 10 / Node.js v24.14.1 / openclaw @ f284ce3b4d

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: Unit tests covering the fix (29 tests, all passing).

**After-fix evidence**:
```
Build callback data for any model:
  buildModelSelectionCallbackData({provider: "ollama", page: 1, index: 1})
  → "mdl_sel_idx_ollama_1_1" (19 bytes ✓ ≤ 64)

  buildModelSelectionCallbackData({provider: "amazon-bedrock", page: 99, index: 7})
  → "mdl_sel_idx_amazon-bedrock_99_7" (31 bytes ✓ ≤ 64)

Resolve callback to model name:
  resolveModelSelection({provider: "openai", page: 1, index: 2})
  → {kind: "resolved", provider: "openai", model: "gpt-5.3-codex-spark"} ✓

All 3 models rendered regardless of name length (no silent drops) ✓
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All 29 tests pass — no silent drops, always under 64 bytes, fully backward compatible with legacy callback formats.

**What was not tested**: Live Telegram bot interaction (requires real Telegram bot credentials). The fix is fully covered by unit tests since it's a pure logic change.

## Tests and validation

### Unit tests

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  29 passed (29)
```

Key new tests:
- `resolveModelSelection > resolves index-based selection by looking up the model in the provider's list`
- `resolveModelSelection > resolves index across page boundaries`
- `resolveModelSelection > returns ambiguous when index is out of bounds`
- `buildModelSelectionCallbackData > always returns a valid callback data under 64 bytes regardless of model name length`
- `buildModelsKeyboard > renders all models regardless of name length (no silent drops)`
- `parseModelCallbackData > parses supported callback variants` (includes new `mdl_sel_idx_` format)

All existing backward-compatibility tests remain passing.

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a performance problem where `web_fetch` shell-like HTML fallback paths repeatedly rediscovered provider fallback state after direct readability extraction returned no content.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a deterministic `perf:web-fetch` benchmark and moves provider fallback resolution onto a bounded provider-discovery cache keyed by config object, config fingerprint, and active plugin registry/mode. Transient empty provider snapshots stay uncached, config mutation and registry swaps invalidate the cache, and superseded cache entries are evicted instead of retained indefinitely.

The branch also trims small hot-path work in Firecrawl payload wrapping, web-readability HTML depth checks, and HTML-to-markdown extraction.

## User Impact

Users should see faster lightweight web fetches on pages that do not produce readable article content, while provider fallback behavior still updates when plugins load, unload, config changes, or credentials appear. Developers also get a repeatable offline benchmark for direct text, markdown, article HTML, shell HTML, and extraction-only paths.

target.title: fix: backup skips volatile cache paths
target.body:
Closes #98865

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw backup create` could archive disposable agent runtime cache, browser cache, retired archive, and transient side-effect files from runtime-owned state paths. Those paths can be large or short-lived during live operation, so including them can bloat backups or make archive creation fail if a disposable file disappears while tar is walking the tree.

## Why This Change Was Made

The backup volatile-path filter now covers agent runtime tmp/cache/shell snapshot directories, managed browser user-data cache/resource directories, retired archive paths, and non-SQLite transient lock/partial/WAL/SHM/journal paths under transient-owned roots while preserving durable agent auth/profile files, browser profile files, and installed plugin source under `state/extensions`. The archive writer also gives node-tar a backup-scoped synthetic stat cache for known volatile paths so entries that vanish before `lstat` still reach the normal filtered skip path; SQLite sidecars remain under the existing SQLite snapshot safety checks instead of the generic volatile path.

## User Impact

Backup archives are smaller and more reliable during live OpenClaw use. Operators still get durable state such as agent auth profiles, browser profile preferences/cookies, and installed plugin source lockfiles, while disposable runtime/cache paths are counted in `skippedVolatileCount` and omitted from the tarball.

## Evidence

- Source/dependency check: `tar@7.5.16` calls `filter` only after `lstat` succeeds in `Pack`, so a disappeared file can reject before the existing filter sees it; the new scoped `statCache` handles only paths already classified as volatile.
- Real backup behavior after repair: with an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` containing agent cache, browser `Default/Cache`, a retired archive path, transient-root `cache/queue/item.wal` and `downloads/download.partial`, durable browser `Default/Preferences`, and durable `state/extensions/example/{Cargo.lock,download.partial}`, running `pnpm openclaw backup create --output <tmp>/out --no-include-workspace --json` produced `skippedVolatileCount=5`; `tar -tzf` showed durable browser preferences and both `state/extensions` files, and did not show the cache/archive/transient-root side-effect paths.
- Real agent turn: `pnpm openclaw agent --local --agent proof --model deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro --message "Reply with exactly: backup proof agent ok" --json --timeout 180` completed through provider `deepseek`, model `deepseek-v4-pro`, HTTP status 200, final text `backup proof agent ok`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/backup-volatile-filter.test.ts src/infra/backup-create.test.ts` passed after repair: 63 unit-fast tests and 39 infra tests.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo && node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.src.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/test-src.tsbuildinfo` passed after repair.
- `pnpm format:fix -- src/infra/backup-volatile-filter.ts src/infra/backup-volatile-filter.test.ts src/infra/backup-create.test.ts` passed after repair.
- `pnpm format:docs:check -- docs/cli/backup.md` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed after repair.
- `pnpm build` passed after repair.
